PREVENTION OF AIR AND WATER POLLUTION
17. Recommendation (Para 20.2)
The Committee opines that apart from providing financial assistance to the State
Governments for Common Effluent Treatment Plants for modernization and capacity expansion, the
Ministry through its nodal agency i.e. Central Pollution Control Board should make sure that
requisite technical assistance may also be provided to the State Governments and Union Territories.
Furthermore, it recommends that Ministry should seriously look into the matter in the case of
polluting industries, which discharge their effluents into river and lakes. There should be imposition
of heavy penalties and closure notices to such Industrial setups, if they fail to install the requisite
effluent treatment plants within a time frame.
Action Taken by the Government
The concept of the Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETP) arose in order to make a
co-operative movement for pollution control. The main objective of the CETPs is to reduce the
treatment cost to be borne by an individual member unit to a minimum while protecting the water
environment to a maximum. Wastewater of CETPs was envisaged to treat the effluent emanating
from the clusters of compatible small-scale industries. A Centrally Sponsored Scheme has been
undertaken by the Government for enabling the Small Scale Industries (SSI) to set up new and
upgrade the existing Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETP) in the country. A scheme for
financial assistance for the CETPs has been formulated as follows:—
State Subsidy — 25% of the total project cost

18
Matching Central Subsidy — 25% of the total project cost
Entrepreneurs contribution — 20% of the total project cost
Loan from financial institutions — 30% of the total project cost
(IDBI, ICCI or any other nationalized Banks, State Industrial Financial Corporation etc.)
CPCB has undertaken a study through National Environmental Engineering Research
Institute (NEERI) entitled ‘Feasibility Studies on Wastewater Management for Textile Sector in
Tirupur and Tannery and Textile Sector in Erode, Tamil Nadu’ on performance evaluation of
Reverse Osmosis Technology and Nano Filtration, which can help in achieving standards of TDS.
For prevention of population in waterbodies i.e. Rivers and Lakes, the polluting industrial
units located along the Rivers and Lakes are monitored regularly by the concerned State Pollution
Control Boards (SPCBs) for setting up of Pollution control devices and appropriate actions are
taken against the defaulting units to ensure compliance. The overall criteria for selection of
industries are the pollution potential (type as well as load) in the sense of the environmental impact
of the discharges, emissions and disposal of hazardous wastes. The inspections of the following
types of industries are undertaken by CPCB:—
• Seventeen Categories of polluting Industries,
• Polluting Industries located along the Rivers and Lakes.
• Industries located in the Twenty four identified problem areas, and
• Hazardous Waste reprocessing industries.
The steps taken against pollution causing industries include:
(i) Enforcement of prescribed environmental standards;
(ii) Regular monitoring for compliance of prescribed environmental norms;
(iii) Issuance of notices/directions to defaulting units for installation of pollution control
devices under the provisions of various Pollution Control Acts; and
(iv) Implementation on the Charter on Corporate Responsibility for Environmental
Protection for 17 Categories of polluting industries.
Total of 1204 grossly polluting industries (discharging 100 Kg/D BOD) have been identified
as on December, 2006, out of which 775 industries have installed Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP)
and are functioning satisfactorily, 314 industries have been closed and 115 are defaulting and facing
legal action.
Comments
The Committee is of the view that strict vigilance on the part of the Ministry is
required to check the problem of water pollution by the various industries and
simultaneously speedy and stringent penal action should also be taken against the industries
that do not comply with the rules.
NATIONAL LAKE CONSERV ATION PLAN
18. Recommendation (Para 21.3)
The Committee understands that it is slow poisoning of the water that is daily killing a part
of the Dal Lake, which has been the major attraction in Kashmir Valley. Most of the pollutants are

19
above the permissible limit as prescribed by the Water Act (Prevention and Control of Pollution)
and also by the Central Board for Control of Pollution (CPCB). Besides, the known factors like
human settlements, hotels, floating gardens and even dhobi ghats on the periphery, are negatively
contributing to the lake’s slow death. It has also been observed that to certain extent source of
phosphates and nitrates, both fertilizers promote eutrophication in the lake water, which may be
attributed to the usage of fertilizers by the farmers. Sewage discharge from surrounding
communities around the lake and its tributaries is also a major reason for pollution in Dal Lake.
The Committee is, therefore, deeply perturbed to note the deteriorating water quality of the Dal
Lake.
Action Taken by the Government
Dal-Nagin Lake, like all other inland water bodies in the country, is beset with problems
arising from both natural and anthropogenic causes. The lake is unique in the sense that this
probably is the only lake where a large number of people live inside the lake carrying out cultivation
in water and land, fishing and discharging their wastes into the water body.
The project of ‘‘Conservation and Management Plan for Dal-Nagin Lake in Srinagar’’ has
already been sanctioned by Government of India in September, 2005 under the National Lake
Conservation Plan for Rs. 298.76 crore, which inter-alia  also includes various measures for
reduction of nutrients (pollutants) to improve the lake eco-system. The project is scheduled for
completion by March, 2010. Implementation of works sanctioned under the project has since been
taken up by the J&K Lakes and Waterways Development Authority, the State implementing agency
for the project, and an expenditure of Rs. 81.70 crore has been incurred till end of August, 2007.
For control of nutrient ingress into the lake (responsible for deterioration of lake water
quality), various actions are being taken up under the project.
(A) Sewerage and Sewage Treatment works and Solid Waste Management
Entry of untreated sewage and solid waste from the peripheral areas and hamlets/
houseboats within the lake has been reckoned as the main factor for eco-degradation
of Dal-Nagin Lake. To address this issue, following achievements have been made till
date by the J&K Lakes and Waterways Development Authority,
(i) Main sewers
Out of 27,851 metres of main sewers envisaged to be laid, 17644 metres of
sewers have been laid to carry the sewage to the STPs in respective zones.
(ii) Remodeling of drains
19,804 metres length of drains have been remodeled out of a total length of 20000
metres envisaged under the project.
(iii) Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs)
Out of 6 STPs (having a total treatment capacity of 36.7 mld) envisaged to be
constructed under the project, 3 STPs based on Fluidized Aerobic Bed (FAB)
technology and having a treatment capacity of 15.2 mld have been commissioned
and are functional. The 3 STPs constructed at Hazratbal (7.5 mld capacity),
Habak (3.2 mld capacity) and Laam (4.5 mld capacity) can treat around
41 per cent  of the total sewage generated along the lake periphery that was
flowing directly into the lake.
(iv) Regarding the hamlets within the lake areas and the habitations not falling in the
command area of the STPs, LCS (low cost sanitation) measures are being
resorted to reduce the lake pollution.

20
(v) Solid Waste Management for the houseboats and hamlets within the lake, including
areas in the immediate periphery of the lake, is being conducted through various
NGOs where-under about 7,500 structures are being serviced on a day-to-day
basis, as a result of which about 9125 cu.m. of solid waste is being managed
annually in collaboration with Srinagar Municipal Corporation.
(B) Catchment Management
Silt coming from the catchment areas through the main feeding source that would
contribute to shallowness of the lake and particulate nutrient build-up is being arrested
in the Telbal Nala Settling Basin (which has been constructed for this purpose) before
entering the lake. The gravity of sediment yield is also declining as anti-erosion
measures in the catchment area of the lake have been initiated.
(C) Weed Management
Selective de-weeding is being done for maintaining water quality and ecology of the
lake.
(D) Dredging
Dredging of shallow areas of the lake is being undertaken to ensure removal of
nutrients from the sediment pool. This has resulted in lake water expanse of about
1 sq.m along the northern shore of the lake having an average depth of about 2.5 m.
(E) Water Circulation
An additional outflow arrangement for the lake via Brari Numbal Lagoon has been
constructed under the project, which improves the lake water circulation and helps to
flush the lake back waters and periphery lake channels.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and desires that the Ministry should ensure that the
water quality of the Dal-Nagin lake improves with the help of various measures undertaken
in this regard.
19. Recommendation Para (21.4)
The Committee is of the strong view that conservation of Dal Lake, which is a lake of
national importance, is an urgent issue. It is a God given ornament of Kashmir V alley and hence
crucial in terms of not only ecology but also from the point of augmenting economic well being
of its people and ensuring peace in the valley. It recommends that provision of proper sewage
facilities will lead to the reduction of the organic loading in the lake to great extent. The Committee
therefore recommends that it is necessary to look into the possibilities such as a common sewerage
system for a cluster of houseboats, sanitary systems in individual units and devices for removal
of the wastes in containers.
Action Taken by the Government
The J&K Lakes and Waterways Development Authority have informed that a comprehensive
scheme for houseboat sanitation has been formulated for implementation.
(i) The houseboats located in the Nagin Basin have been realigned along its eastern and
western shore. The sewer line for connecting houseboats on eastern shore has been
laid through which sewage of the houseboats shall be pumped to the STP located at
Hazratbal. The sewage from houseboats on western side of Nagin Lake shall be
connected to sewer for carrying the same to the STP proposed to be constructed at
Nala Amir Khan.

21
(ii) The houseboats located in the Nehru Park Basin of Dal Lake shall be provided with
floating septic tanks and Vacussun sewer system. The pre-requisite of this scheme
requires relocation and realignment of houseboats in the lake, the proposals of which
have been finalized and the dredging of the area on the western side of the lake near
Kohnakhun for providing mooning sites for these houseboats has been undertaken. 32
houseboats have so far been relocated in the area carved out.
Comments
The Committee while taking note of the reply is of the view that the comprehensive
sewage and sanitation system formulated should be put in place expeditiously and the
results monitored.
20. Recommendation (Para 21.5)
The Committee in its earlier report on action taken by the Ministry of Environment and
Forests on the recommendations contained in report of the Committee on ‘Conservation and
Environmental Management Plan for Dal-Nagin Lake’ had further recommended the Ministry to take
initiatives to import Rota Loo, lightweight portable toilet aided by hundred per cent biodegradable
toilet bag which is compostable and is not only environmental friendly but also user friendly. The
Committee, therefore, again recommends for Rota Loo toilets, which could also be used on the
houseboats in Dal Lake. It would like the Ministry to furnish details of actions taken in this
context, as the aerobic breakdown of human wastes in a biodrum is the most advisable technique
for preventing the inflow of human wastes into the lake eco-system.
Action Taken by the Government
The J&K Lakes and Waterways Development Authority have informed that the proposal of
using ‘‘Rota Loo’’ toilets as well as other alternatives like ‘‘Envirolet’’ biolet units for houseboats
has already been considered and evaluated by them. However, both these options were not
recommended for the following reasons:
(a) Both these units are more specifically designed for situations where water is scarce but
power is abundant. The conditions in case of Dal Lake were found to be opposite.
(b) Waste in such units is composted in pits, which is neither possible nor desirable in the
lake.
(c) The Rota Loo toilets are to be operated manually, which is not possible in houseboat
condition.
(d) The costs involved in both types are prohibitive.
A meeting of Board of Directors of the J&K Lakes and Waterways Development Authority
on this matter was held on 24.9.2005, wherein it was decided to adopt ‘Floating Septic Tanks’ with
Vacussun sewer system for discharging the liquid waste of houseboats into the terminal shore
sump-cum-pump station for ultimate treatment in the existing/proposed STPs for scientific
houseboat sanitation. The J&K Lakes and Waterways Development Authority have informed that
since the Parliamentary Committee has recommended re-examining the utility of ‘‘Rota Loo’’ toilets
in the houseboats, they will re-examine the matter.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and desires that an effective method for disposal of
wastes from the Houseboats in the Dal Lake is put in place within a fixed time schedule.
The Committee would like to be apprised of the steps being taken towards this.

22
GREGARIOUS FLOWERING OF MULl BAMBOOS
21. Recommendation (Para 23.3)
The Committee appreciates the efforts initiated by the Ministry to tap the ecological, social
and economic problems likely to arise due to gregarious flowering of muli bamboos. It recommends
that Ministry must keep up its efforts to ensure that the resources and huge amount of funds
involved in this project are managed properly and effectively.
Action Taken by the Government
To tackle the ecological, social and economic problems likely to arise due to gregarious
flowering of Bamboo, the Ministry of Environment and Forests (MoEF), GoI is implementing a
Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS), under which following steps have been taken:—
(i) The Comprehensive Action Plan was approved on July 20, 2005. The Scheme has
been finally approved on March 30, 2006 by the Planning Commission and the
Ministry of Finance for implementation from 2005-06 to 2008-09.
(ii) Under this CSS, seven NE States and ICFRE are being financially supported as per
the approved Action Plan. The main activities for which the funds will be utilized are:
• Improvement of link roads for bamboo extraction/regeneration;
• Creation of transit depots/collection centres;
• Purchase of vehicles for monitoring and staff mobility;
• Mechanized ropeways to facilitate extraction of bamboo;
• Regeneration activities;
• Fire-control measures;
• Rodent control;
• Preventive health measures;
• Utilizing bamboo for bio-energy by gasification; and
• Disposal of unutilized bamboo by burning.
(iii) The seven States are: Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram,
Nagaland and Tipura.
(iv) The total expected requirement of fund for implementation of the Action Plan has
been estimated as Rs 366.50 crores, out of which the MoEF, is supplementing the
efforts of the State Governments and ICFRE, concerned through by an estimated
budget of Rs. 85.00 crores for total project period.
(v) During Financial Year (FY) 2005-06, an amount of Rs 17.82 crores has been released
to different NE States and ICFRE to combat the problems. In the FY 2006-07, the
total amount released is Rs 25.00 crores and for the current FY , the estimated budget
to be released is Rs 27.00 crores out of which Rs. 6.28 crores has been released so
far to the implementing States.
(vi) A Central M onitoring Committee (CMC) under the chairmanship of Director General
of Forests and Special Secretary (DGF&SS), MoEF, Government of India has been
constituted on August 31, 2004, which includes PCCFs/Forest Secretaries of the State
Governments, representatives from Ministry of Agriculture, DONER, National Mission
on Bamboo Application (NMBA), North-Eastern Council (NEC) and Planning
Commission.

23
(a) This Committee held bimonthly meeting to review the progress of the scheme.
So far CMC has held six CMC meetings; the next one is scheduled to be held
on September 18, 2007 at Guwahati, Assam.
(vii) The major consumer of bamboo produce is HPC. No States report to export of
bamboos to Bangladesh except Tripura. Bamboo produce is being properly utilized for
Paper and Pulp Industry, Handicrafts, Construction/Structural purposes, Bio-energy,
Incense stick, Umbrella handle etc.
(viii) The National Mission on Bamboo Applications (NMBA), Ministry of Science and
Technology is helping the implementing States in providing technical know-how and
financial assistance to the local entrepreneurs for setting up Gasifiers, activated
charcoal units, stick making units providing quality nursery stocks for regeneration.
(ix) MoEF decided to give dispensation from felling restrictions to Muli Bamboos till
gregarious flowering is over. The States can do harvesting without approved working
plans/schemes by developing some mechanism at the State level to ensure proper
harvesting and utilization.
(a) The export restrictions on muli bamboos have been lifted till March, 2008.
Comments
Committee acknowledges the various efforts undertaken by the Ministry to minimize
the problems likely to arise due to flowering of the muli bamboos and hopes that these
efforts would bear fruit.
22. Recommendation (Para 24)
After examining the various aspects of Demand for Grants of the Ministry of Environment
and Forests, the Committee observed that the budget allocation for the year 2007-08 has not been
made with the realistic perception with the result that the Ministry would not be in a position to
complete its ongoing schemes/programmes with such allocations. The Committee also felt that the
major activities/programmes like national afforestation programme, the functioning of Botanical
Survey of India/Zoological Survey of India, filling up of vacant posts in various grades in various
organizations under the purview of the Ministry and creation of scientists pool etc. would suffer
because of the tight budgetary provisions. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry
should seek for more allocations at R.E stage for various ongoing projects/programmes so that the
Ministry can deliver better environment inputs which the country needs in the wake of prevailing
environmental degradation.
Action Taken by the Government
The low budgetary allocations in 2007-08 Budget of the Ministry is mainly on account of
only a marginal increase in the plan budget of the Ministry. This was due to reduction in approved
plan outlay of the Ministry by Rs. 70 crores by the Planning Commission, for salary and
establishment related expenditure, as a part of its zero-Budget Based exercise and transfer of the
same to non plan budget of the Ministry. While the reduction in plan budget was effected by the
Planning Commission, its concomitant enhancement in Ministry’s non plan Budget was not effected
by the Finance Ministry.
The requirements of plan funds by various schemes/projects will be assessed, as a part of
Ministry’s mid-year review exercise. Given the progress in utilization of funds and the additional
requirements of funds, if any, necessary demand for additional funds will be made to Finance
Ministry for various schemes/projects at R.E. stage.

24
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and desires that it be apprised of the changes, if any,
that were effected at the R.E. Stage.

PREFACE
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and
Technology, Environment and Forests, having been authorised by the Committee to present the
Report on its behalf, present this One Hundred Eighty-fifth report of the Committee. This Report
deals with the detailed Demands for Grants (2008-09) of the Department of Science and
Technology (Ministry of Science and Technology) (Demand No.83).
2. In the meeting of the Committee held on the 25th March, 2008, the Secretary and other
Officers of the Department of Science and Technology gave an overview of the various activities
of the Department and the Members sought clarifications on various aspects of the performance
of the Department to enable it to scrutinise the Demands for Grants.
3. The Committee express its thanks to the Officers of the Department for replying to the
clarifications sought by the Members and placing before it the required material to enable the
Committee to scrutinise the Demands for Grants of the Department of Science and Technology.
4. The Committee considered and adopted the Report at its meeting held on the 23rd April, 2008.
DR. V . MAITREYAN
N
EW D ELHI; Chairman,
April 23, 2008 Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on
Science and Technology, Environment and Forests.

1
REPORT
India is a land of one of the oldest civilizations of the world with a rich cultural heritage,
thriving economy and civic life. It has been a fountainhead of ancient knowledge and wisdom. The
traditions of science and technology in India are over 5000 years old. The resurgence of science
in India came as an offshoot of the Nationalist Movement, towards the end of 19th century and
the early decades of the 20th century. Since 1947 a renaissance was witnessed with the emergence
of India as a politically independent nation and as it pursued a programme of employing modern
Science and Technology for national development. A few exceptionally talented and committed
scientists and teachers of that period laid down the foundations of Indian science with their zeal,
dedication and sacrifice. Conscious efforts were made to enhance and modernize the scientific
infrastructure in the country by establishing a series of national laboratories, institutes of advanced
technical education, universities, etc. Science and Technology inputs were made an intrinsic part
of the planning process and development strategies. Many institutions were created soon after
independence to promote basic research and technological progress.
1.1 The Department of Science and Technology was established with the primary objective to
give fillip to promotion of new areas of Science and Technology and to play the role of a nodal
Department for organizing, coordinating and promoting S&T activities in the country.
1.2 Over the years, the investments in S&T sector have gone up consistently and significantly.
From an allocation of Rs. 349 crores in the Seventh Plan to the Department of Science and
Technology, it went up to Rs. 1192 crores in the Eighth Plan, Rs. 1497 crores in the Ninth Plan,
Rs. 3400 crores in the Tenth Plan to Rs.11028 crores in the Eleventh Five Year Plan. Provision
proposed in the Plan outlay for the year 2008-09 was Rs. 1800 crores, however, the allocation
made by the Planning Commission is Rs.1530 crores which is Rs. 270 crores less than the
projected demand by the Department. The Committee was informed that the Department has been
assured that additional funds would be made available based on performance assessment at the R.E.
stage.
1.3 The detailed budget allocation of the Department of Science and Technology for
the financial year 2008-09 was considered by the Department-related Parliamentary
Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and Forests at its meeting held on
25th March, 2008 and the Demands for Grants of the Department provided the following
provisions.
2. BUDGETARY ALLOCATIONS
2.1 The Budgetary Estimates of the Department of Science and Technology for the year
2008-09 are placed at Rs. 1780.00 crores (Plan Rs. 1530.00 crores and Non-Plan Rs. 250.00
crores) as compared to last year’s B.E. and R.E. of Rs. 1775.00 crores and Rs. 1511.00 crores
respectively. The percentage increase in B.E. 2008-09 over the B.E. 2007-08 is only 0.28% i.e.,
from Rs. 1775.00 crores to Rs. 1780.00 crores.
2.2 The Committee has been informed that the Department’s plan outlay of Rs. 1526
crores at the BE stage last year was reduced to Rs. 1270 crores at the RE stage. The
Department, however, was unable to spend even the reduced Grants during the last year.
The Committee takes serious note of the situation and recommends that the Department
should be more prompt and efficient in utilising the allocated funds. This acquires even
more importance because the rise in allocation this year, the committee feels, is miniscule,
if put in the context of inflation and economic growth. At the same time the Committee

2
is of the opinion that, keeping in mind the responsibilities of the Department and the role
it is expected to play in development of science and technology, the Department should be
given an increase in allocation in consonance with its requirements.
3. PROGRAMMES OF THE DEPARTMENT IN ELEVENTH FIVE YEAR PLAN
3.1 The list of various programmes to be carried out by the Department in Eleventh Five Year
Plan is as follows:
Sl. Name of the Scheme/Project/Programme
No.
1 Research and Development Support
2 Technology Development Programme
3 S&T Programme for Socio-economic Development
4 International Cooperation
5 State Science and Technology Programme
6 Modernization of Mapping Organizations (SoI & NATMO)
7 Autonomous Institutions and Professional Bodies
8 V ocational Employment Generation
9 Technology for Bamboo Products (Mission Mode Project)
10 Synergy Projects (O/o Pr. Scientific Adviser)
11 Information Technology
12 National Training Programme for Scientists/Technologists Working with Government
of India
13 Drugs and Pharmaceuticals Research
14 National Mission on Nano-science and Nano-technology
15 Science and Engineering Research Board
16 Scholarships for Science in Higher Education (Oversight Committee Recommendation)
17 Water Technology Initiative
18 Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research ( INSPIRE)
19 Innovation Clusters
20 Security Technology Initiative
21 Mega Facilities for Basic Research
4. MECHANISMS TO MONITOR AND REVIEW THE PROGRESS OF ONGOING
SCHEME
4.1 The Committee has been informed that to monitor and review the progress of its ongoing
schemes before formulating/finalizing proposals for budgetary support, each scheme has an Expert
Advisory Committee to assist the department. This mechanism has been there in place and is well
established.

3
4.2 The Committee welcomes the constitution of Expert Advisory Committees to monitor
and review the progress of its ongoing schemes and is of the opinion that such a step can
be helpful in prioritization and rationalisation of schemes.
5. SHIFTING AND RESTRUCTURING OF PROGRAMMES
5.1 The Department has informed that Programmes such as India Meteorological Department
(IMD), National Council for Medium Range and Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF) and some
programmes related to Seismology have been shifted to the new Ministry of Earth Sciences. Some
internal restructuring of programmes and schemes has also been done.
6. Research and Development Support
6.1 The Department of Science and Technology, as a part of its S&T promotional activity has
been supporting R&D programmes under Science and Engineering Research Council (SERC). The
objectives of the SERC are:—
(i) To promote research in newly emerging and frontline areas of Science and Engineering
including multidisciplinary fields;
(ii) To selectively promote general research capability in relevant areas of Science and
Engineering taking into account existing research capabilities of the host institution; and
(iii) To encourage young scientists to take up challenging research and development
activities.
6.2 The allocation for ‘Research and Development Support to Multi-disciplinary Research in
Science and Technology’ which stood at Rs. 346.50 crores in Budget 2007-08 was increased to
Rs. 371.37 crores at the Revision Estimates Stage and has been now been increased to Rs.417.00
crores in Budget 2008-09.
6.3 The Committee has been informed that the department is committed to the pursuit
and promotion of science & technology with vigour in the Eleventh Five Year Plan. SERC, which
is the single largest basic research funding mechanism in the country across disciplines and
institutions, has intensified the R&D promotional activities through innovative programmes such
as Intensification of Research in High Priority Areas (IRHPA), Fund for Improvement of S&T
Infrastructure in Universities and Higher Educational Institutions (FIST), Fast Track Young
Scientist's R&D programme and Prestigious Fellowships like J.C. Bose, Ramanujan, Ramanna, etc.
The budget allocation of Rs. 417.00 crore in 2008-09 includes the allocation for the proposed
Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB).
7. SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING RESEARCH COUNCIL (SERC)
7.1 The objective of the Council is to promote research in newly emerging and frontier areas
of science and engineering including multidisciplinary fields; selectively promote the general
research capability in relevant areas of science and engineering taking into account capability of the
host institute; encourage young scientists to take up challenging R&D activities; give special
encouragement to projects from less endowed university departments; encourage patenting facilities
to scientists and technologists in the country for Indian and foreign patents on a sustained basis;
promote basic and applied research in frontline areas of engineering and technology in various
academic and research institutions, in collaboration with industry and user agencies (where
applicable), and to transfer such technologies for developmental activities; create and strengthen
S&T infrastructure in Universities and National Institutes; Creation of core groups/ units around an
outstanding scientist; take steps to widen, in general, the base of scientific R&D in the country
by attracting the best available talent to pursue research as career, by spreading R&D culture in

4
universities and other higher educational institutions at large and by taking all other necessary
promotional measures.
7.2 The Secretary of the Department during the presentation made to the Committee
has informed that Science and Engineering Research Council (SERC) needs an increase in
allocation of about 25% in order to fulfil its objectives. The Committee, keeping in mind
the huge array of responsibilities for promotion of research in newly emerging and frontier
areas of science and engineering including multidisciplinary fields; need for encouraging
young scientists to take up challenging R&D activities and imperatives to promote basic and
applied research in frontline areas of engineering and technology in various academic and
research institutions, etc., among many others, recommends that sufficient budgetary
support may be provided so that the programme could be pursued with vigour.
7.3 The Committee has been informed that around 3000 research proposals are received
by the Department every year out of which 500-600 proposals are selected for funding. The
Committee is of the view that lack of fund should not be allowed to come in the way of
funding good and promising research proposals.
8. SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY PROGRAMMES FOR SOCIO-ECONOMIC
DEVELOPMENT
8.1 The Societal Programme of the Department plays a vital role in the development strategy
of various sections of the society, which provides opportunities to motivate scientists, engineers
and field level workers to take-up time bound developmental projects with inputs of Science and
Technology for the benefit of disadvantaged sections of the society. The programmes are being
implemented through S&T institutions, universities and S&T based voluntary organizations under
various schemes.
8.2 The following plan schemes: Science and Technology Entrepreneurship Development,
Science & Society Programme, Women Component Plan, S&T Communication & Popularization
and other schemes: (i) Special Component Plan for the Development of Scheduled Castes,
(ii) Tribal Sub-plan which were hitherto separate plan schemes have now been merged and renamed
as S&T Programme for Socio Economic Development insofar as budget outlays are concerned.
8.3 The success of Science can be gauged by the fact as to how far it has been able to
touch and ameliorate the life and lot of one and all. The committee feels that going by this
yardstick a lot more is desired to be done. The committee is of the opinion that science
should come out of the confines of laboratories to make its outreach to the common masses
and it needs to be done in a time bound manner or a sustained basis. This becomes all the
more imperative as India needs to shed its tag of a developing nation and acquire the
stature of a developed one, the sooner the better, and it is none other but science which
holds the magic stick to do wonders. DST being the nodal Ministry, the onus lies with it.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department of Science and Technology
should coordinate with all other scientific departments and institutions to move forward in
this direction and lay more and more emphasis on S&T programme for socio-economic
development.
9. TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME
9.1 The programme is aimed at developing indigenous technology through joint projects with
industry and socio-economic Ministries. It also includes activities relating to Development of
Natural Resources Data Management System, Patent Facilitating Cells, Instrument Development
Programme, Technology Projects in Mission Mode, Joint Technology Projects and Drugs and
Pharmaceuticals Research.

5
9.2 Technology Development Board (TDB) has been set up to help the indigenously developed
technologies reach the stage of commercial application and for grafting imported technologies for
wider domestic applications.
9.3 Allocation for payment to Technology Development Board against Cess receipts has been
hiked from Rs.19.00 crores at R.E. Stage in 2007-08 to Rs. 20.80 crores in 2008-09. The
Committee has been informed that during the year 2007-08, BE for Technology Development Board
was Rs. 20.80 crores under non-plan. There was a mandatory cut of 5% on non plan expenditure.
This was, therefore, reduced to 19.00 crores at RE stage. During the year 2008-09, it has been
projected at the level of BE (2007-08) and hence BE for 2008-09 is Rs. 20.80 crores.
9.4 The committee acknowledges the important role that TDP plays in translating lab-
scale research into technology mode but for which the benefit of science cannot be reaped.
The Committee, therefore, desires that Technology Development Programmes should be
further strengthened and intensified so that the advantages of new breakthroughs in the
field of science could be taken to the masses at the earliest and at an affordable cost.
9.5 The Committee is also of the view that developing indigenous technology through
joint projects is also of utmost importance because without industry participation such
projects will not only become exorbitant but also lack the commercial dimension which is
very important for successful culmination of such projects.
10. MODERNISATION OF MAPPING ORGANIZATIONS (SOI AND NATMO)
10.1 Survey of India (SOl) and National Atlas and Thematic Mapping Organization (NATMO) are
operationally two different entities, but insofar as the budget outlays are concerned the two
schemes have been merged and renamed as ‘Modernisation of Mapping Organizations’. The
National Atlas and Thematic Mapping Organization set up in 1956 primarily aims at preparing
National Atlas of India. Subsequently, its scope and activities were extended to new fields of
geographical research, thematic mapping covering all the academic and applied aspects of
geography and allied subjects.
10.2 Allocation to the tune of 195.60 crores was made in Budget 2007-08 for ‘Modernization
of Mapping Organisation’ (SOI and NATMO). It has been reduced to 185.37 crores in Budget
2008-09. It is stated that the budgetary allocation under the Revenue section during 2007-08 was
Rs. 195.38 crore for both National Atlas and Thematic Maping Organisation (NATMO) and Survey
of India (SOI) under the scheme ‘Modernization of Mapping Organisation. This has been reduced
to Rs. 190.255 crore in the Budgetary allocation for 2008-09. This is only a marginal difference
in Budget allocation and shall be reviewed at the RE stage.
10.3 The Committee is of the view that the mapping work should not suffer as a result
of inadequacy of funds, as it plays an important role in planning of resource utilization and
other schemes.

12. SYNERGY PROJECTS

7
catalytic role in taking up selective R&D and technology development projects in a number of

edge research.
13. NATIONAL TRAINING PROGRAMME
13.1 National Training Programme for Scientists/Technologists working with the Government of
India, is an initiative undertaken with a view to provide holistic training and empowering them with
capabilities. The programmes are categorised broadly to cater to General Management Development
Areas, specific and highly specialized areas, techno-scientific management covering multi-
disciplinary areas, etc.
13.2 Fresh allocation to the tune of Rs. 5.00 crores has been made in budget 2008-2009 for

Government of India. The Committee has been informed that in 2007-2008 the Department of

(b) Integrated Middle level Training Programmes (5 weeks)-one
(c) Senior Scientists Techno-Scientific Management Programme (2 weeks)-one
(d) Senior Scientist General Management Programme (2 weeks)-one

Expenditure budget V olume II.
13.5 The Committee welcomes the initiative of the Department to upgrade the skills of
its scientists by conducting various training programmes which will certainly enable them
to meet contemporary standards and overcome any difficulties arising out of lack of

at RE stage so that some more training programmes may be added under this scheme.
14. DRUGS AND PHARMACEUTICAL PROGRAMME
14.1 The scheme is to be used for the purpose of supporting research and development
programmes and setting up of national facilities for furthering R&D activities in the country and
for defining areas of relevance and value to the Indian populace and intensifying the work in such
areas by synergizing the core competence of the constituents (publicly funded R&D institutions and
the Indian Pharmaceutical industry).

8
14.2 Allocation made to ‘Drugs and Pharamaceutical Research’ has been reduced to Rs.100.00
crores in Budget 2008-09 from Rs.118.00 crores in Budget 2007-08. The Committee has been
informed that allocation of Rs.118 crores at BE/RE for 2007-08 was made at a time when the
Eleventh plan was under finalization. Subsequently, Eleventh plan was finalized and the allocation
for Drug and Pharma programme for the plan period is Rs. 500 crores. Accordingly, for the year
2008-09, 100 crores has been provided.
14.3 The Committee is of the view that in a country where poverty is rampant and
substantial part of population suffers from diseases, a continued effort in drug research is
required for providing cheaper medicines. Continued support to drug research programmes
should be provided to enable the scientists to find cheaper and effective drugs. The
Committee recommends that drug research programmes should focus on diseases which are
afflicting the large populace of our country.
14.4 In its 162nd report on Drugs and Pharmaceuticals Research Programme including the herbal
medicines the Committee had observed that ‘‘On herbal research, as a short-term strategy, there
is a need to develop medicines to combat most prevalent diseases like Gastric problems, Arthritis,
Diabetes, Stress Related Disorders, Thoracic Diseases, etc., for which a well thought strategy
requires to be evolved. Time bound research on herbal drugs may be a suitable option. It was
informed that a large number of ISM drugs are being used for a long time, having no acute
toxicity. But long-term toxicity on these drugs must be established. A few more experiments could
be done in scientific manner to make it more meaningful. Public sector units may be utilized for
production of these drugs for mass consumption.’’ In its Action Taken Note on the same the
Government has replied that Studies related to scientific validation along with toxicity and efficacy
studies of certain herbal formulations besides certain herbo-mineral formulations are being carried
out under various programmes of Government of India.
14.5 The Committee reiterates it earlier recommendation that more efforts should be
made to make alternative system of medicines successfully fill in the gap in areas where
conventional cures are not available. The Committee felt that research in Traditional/
Alternative systems should focus on areas where conventional cures are either inadequate
or too costly.

15.1 The following areas of research have been identified for immediate attention :
• Studies of free atomic and molecular clusters, cluster assembled materials, low-
dimensional structures and quantum dots;
• Nano-electronics and nano-photonics
• Applications; nano-coatings, nano-device based sensors and diagnostics kits, controlled
and targeted drug delivery systems, nano-phosphor based display devices, etc.
15.2 Allocation to ‘National Mission on nano Sciences and Nano Technology’ had been decreased
from Rs. 150.00 crores in Budget 2007-08 to Rs. 120.00 crores at R.E. state. The allocation has
been enhanced to Rs. 145.00 crores in Budget 2008-09. The Committee has been informed that
a new. programme ‘‘National Mission on Nano Science and Technology (nano Mission)’ has been
allocated Rs. 150.00 crores in the BE stage. Based on the National consultation on Nano Mission,
the government has approved the implementation of nano Mission on May 3, 2007. The Mission
has many components such as basic research promotion & HRD programmes, Nano Technology
Application Programmes which look into Joint Industry-Academia/National lab R&D Projects,
Establishing nano Application & Technology Development Centres, nano-Technology Business

9
Incubators etc., International collaborations: Joint Centres in specific areas etc. These activities
have to be implemented in phases. A Mission management has to be put in place.
15.3 A Nano M ission council (NMC) has only recently been constituted. The technical
programmes of the Nano Mission are also being guided by two advisory groups, viz. the nano
Science Advisory Group (NSAG) and the nano Applications and Technology Advisory Group
(NATAG). Both the groups have been constituted. Several proposals have been identified for
support. It was recommended to establish three major Institutes of Nano Science and Technology
in the country with each costing approximately Rs. 100 crores. PG Teaching Programmes (M.Sc./
M.Tech.) in Nano Science and Technology has been initiated.11 Universities/institutes have been
identified in the first batch.
15.4 The Committee welcomes the proposal to establish three major Institutes of Nano
Science and Technology and the introduction of PG Teaching Programmes (M.Sc./M.Tech.) in
Nano Science and Technology. The Committee is of the view that such proactive steps are
required for creating a pool of scientists to cater to the needs of this unfolding research
frontier which holds immense potential for the future.
16. SCHOLARSHIPS FOR SCIENCE IN HIGHER EDUCATION (SHE)
16.1 Scholarship for Higher Education (SHE) is an innovative scheme aimed at attracting the
bright students in the age group of 17-22 year who have passed their Grade X and Grade XII
examinations with excellent marks. The Scheme offers Rs. 1 lakh per year for continuing science
education at B.Sc. and M.Sc. levels for 10,000 candidates per year. This will be linked with the
other two components of the INSPIRE program.
16.2 Allocat ion to ‘Scholarships for Science in higher Education’ has been decreased from
Rs. 100.00 crores in Budget 2007-08 to Rs. 85.00 crores in Budget 2008-09. The scheme aims
at an annual accretion of 10,000/- ‘best in class’ future researchers per year, which should enable
India to become a Global player in R&D. In this way a class of best young brains of the country
can be nurtured and retained for research in science streams. This would eventually enable India
to embark on ambitious course of wealth creation through IPR generation. The Department has
prepared the Detailed Proposal and has approached the Expenditure Finance Committee for
approval. Part of the fellowship is in cash and remaining as attachments like for attending national
(BSc & MSc Level) & international (at MSc Level only) conferences, Book etc. Therefore in the
first year (2007-08) an allocation of Rs. 85.0 crore i.e. 85% of the cost of 10,000 fellowships is
sufficient for effective implementation.
16.3 The Committee appreciates the scheme and is of the view that the above programme
is a step taken in right direction and more such programmes are required to initiate and
retain students in the field of science. The Committee feels that funds should not be
allowed to be an obstacle as the future of science and of the country rests on such small
beginnings which will have crucial effects on the future.
16.4 The Committee feels that the geographical reach of SHE should also be extended to
distant parts of the country like Ladakh and the Northeast and other backward States. The
Committee has also been informed that the Department was unable to implement the ‘SHE’
scheme because it required consultation and approval of several departments. The
Committee recommends that the Department expedite the process of consultation along
with other Departments for speedy execution of proposals. Beside this the Committee also
recommends that a special effort should be made to increase the reach of the programmes
to students who are not as advantaged as in the Metros but are equally deserving and this
should specially take into consideration girl students who are unable to take advantage of
opportunities.

10

17.2 Allocation to 'Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research’ has been decreased from

building innovative knowledge infrastructure by conversion of comparative strength of India by
virtue of its demography and inherited knowledge systems into competitive advantage. The scheme,
which offers science as a career option by providing necessary opportunities for youth, has the
following components:

Early Attracting of Talents for Science (SEATS) and Assured Opportunity for Research
Careers (AORC) in the age group of 22-32 years for 5 years doctoral research backed by

focus on its core competencies rather than spreading its resources too thin. The top-most
priority should be given to tapping young talent through various monetary and motivational
schemes. Stress should be laid on ‘catching them young’
18. WATER TECHNOLOGY INITIATIVE
18.1 The focus of the program is on design and development of low cost solutions for domestic
use of technologies for safe drinking water. Since quality is the main consideration of safe drinking
water research, such technologies are being focused. The initiative would include also the pilot
testing of a credible number of products and referencing of selected technologies to the social
contexts of the application regions.
18.2 Allocation to ‘Water Technology Initiative’ has been increased from Rs. 00.60 crores in
Budget 2007-08 to Rs.5.00 crores in Budget 2008-2009. The Committee has been informed that
the BE for Water Technology Initiative was Rs. 5 crores during the year 2007-08. As this is a new
initiative under the Eleventh Plan and 2007-08 was the initial year, it took some time to gear up

11
the activities after completing the administrative/financial procedural requirements. So, at RE stage,
it was reduced to 0.60 crores. During the year 2008-09, the programme is expected to run at its
full swing, in terms of up gradation/dissemination of technologies like nano-coated candles
developed by ARCI (Hyderabad), low cost candle filters developed by RRL (Bhubanesvar).
18.3 When the Committee enquired about the research work developed in removing fluoride and
arsenic from water in different parts of the country, the Secretary, Department of Science and
Technology has informed that CSIR has developed a technology for removal of hazardous minerals.
It was also informed that the Department has already developed necessary base for the
development of technology for the removal of various hazardous and harmful containments such
as arsenic, fluoride, iron and dissolved salts. Sixteen iron removal plants based on the ceramic
membranes have been supported in the north-eastern states. Fifteen more such plants are on the
anvil to cater to the requirement of Nagaland. Completion of development of arsenic removal
systems through microbial as well as innovative chemical processes is likely to be completed after
rigorous field tests. The sea water desalination units have been successfully installed at
Ramanathapuram district of Tamil Nadu. This technology is upscaled using heat recovery system
to cater to the requirements of other areas devoid of potable drinking water.
18.4 T he Committee is of the opinion that a project for development of low cost filters
for domestic purposes should be given top-most priority as millions of households in this
country, for want of affordable filters, suffer from waterborne diseases. Integrating effective
technologies to purify drinking water supplied by civic authorities is yet another challenge
to be taken by the Department in larger interest. The Committee would also like the
Department to enter into partnership with Industry so as to make such products
commercial and popular.
18.5 The Committee is also of the opinion that such water treatment technology should
be made available in large scale catering to the needs at community level and arsenic,
fluoride, iron and other hazardous minerals should be removed before it reaches
households. The Committee is of the further view that there is an urgent need to develop
models which would be low cost, low power consuming and which can benefit people of
different parts of the country afflicted by the problem.
19. INNOV ATION CLUSTERS
19.1 Whereas the education and industrial infrastructure in the country are developing side by
side there is a need to develop an innovation infrastructure to link knowledge products to the
generation of wealth. It is also necessary to mount such an initiative under an effective public-
private partnership model in areas where the trade and advantages have already been established and
the clustering processes are evident. Evidence based selection of the sectors and locations for
innovation clusters will be essential.
19.2 Allocation to ‘Innovation clusters’ has been increased from Rs.1.80 crores in R.E.
2007-08 Rs.5.00 crores in Budget 2008-09. The Committee has been informed that innovation
Clusters is a new scheme proposed for implementation in the Eleventh Five Year Plan. Since
2007-08 was the first year of the Plan, therefore R.E. was kept at Rs.1.8 crores. Necessary
approvals for implementation of the scheme are being sought during the current financial year.
During 2008-09 the implementation of the scheme is expected to be in full swing and therefore
the allocation has been increased to Rs.5.00 crores.
19.3 The Committee is of the opinion that an innovation infrastructure to link knowledge
products to the generation of wealth is of immense importance in knowledge economy. Rich
fruits of research should also be commercially viable to sustain themselves and encourage

12
further research. Innovation clusters benefiting the academy and industrial sectors under
an effective public-private partnership model is the need of the hour for future successes
of research initiatives.
20. SECURITY TECHNOLOGY INITIATIVES
20.1 Internal security is a subject of concern in modern civilizations in many countries and hence
a science and technology initiative in this area is essential. This technology however, involves a
careful selection and symbiosis of many disciplines. Since Department of Science and Technology
enjoys the benefit of linkages with a vast network of institutions, it has already made a preliminary
attempt to structure and implement the national initiative. A new national program is being proposed
using the NMITLI type model.
20.2 Allocation to ‘Security Technology Initiative’ has decreased from Rs 10.00 crores in Budget
2007-08 to Rs 5.00 crores in Budget 2008-09. The Committee has been informed that the
department is committed to pursuing its aim of development of technologies and other S&T
interventions for ‘Security’ purposes. In order to prepare a user-oriented and user-driven process
of evolving technologies some ground work needs to be done by this Department which is planned
in June/July, 2008. Subsequently such projects would be evolved. In view of the involvement of
few agencies and the time required to evolve user-oriented proposals it is felt that the initial
expenditure would be low and hence the reduction in the budget. The Committee is of the opinion
that in a world where security has been inextricably linked with technology, the country require
sophisticated technology for both intelligence gathering and security. Effective research initiatives
and adequate funds for the same should be provided at all costs. This initiative becomes all the
more imperative as our country is confronting the menace of all sorts of terrorism sported from
outside the border of the country.
20.3 The convergence of technology and security issues is indicative of the highly
technological world we are living in. Technology not only determines how we live our lives
but also how we protect ourselves from negative forces determined to destroy our social and
economic fabric. It is here that the Committee feels that technology has an important role
to play in intelligence gathering as well as monitoring internal security situation and it
urges that the Department should do all that is possible to achieve breakthroughs in
security technology in a time bound manner so that we could be in a position to effectively
tackle the threats posed to our internal security and improve our intelligence gathering
capabilities.
21. MEGA FACILITIES FOR BASIC RESEARCH
21.1 Basic research in the country has been depending upon mega and capital intensive facilities
created by other countries. This practice has led to asymmetries in credit sharing. DST alongwith
DAE has identified areas where an effective partnership of the two departments can bring about
an effective capacity building in the university and academic sector for creating mega faculties for
basic research.
21.2 Allocation to ‘Mega facilities for Basic Research’ bas been reduced from Rs. 25.00 crores
in 2007-08 to Rs. 20.00 crores in 2008-09. The Committee has been informed that the scheme
aims at creation of mega science programmes and facilities in and out side the country to improve
access to such state-of-the,.art facilities to the Indian scientific community, especially from the
academic sector.
21.3 Since the scheme requires the involvement of various stake holders including other
Scientific Departments like DAE, DBT etc. and International community, a. marginally low initial
expenditure is expected. Several proposals like Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research (Germany),

13
Japan beam line for materials research, ELETRA beam line etc. are in advanced stages for
implementation in 2008-09.
21.4 The Committee welcomes the symbiotic research initiative taken by the Department
along with Department of Atomic Energy (DAE). Identification of areas where an effective
partnership of the two departments can bring about an effective capacity building in the
university and academic sector for building mega faculties for basic research is of utmost
importance as it is a known fact that without progress in basic science, technological
progress cannot. sustain itself for very long.
21.5 The Committee has been informed -that the Department has developed a soil-testing kit,
which costs Rs. 3000 per unit. The Committee would like the Department to popularise the kit
among farmers and rope in Industry to promote the product. The Committee also recommends that
the Department should coordinate with the Ministry of Agriculture to promote its uses among the
farmers. It also recommends that at least one soil testing kit be made available free of cost at the
Panchayat or Village level so that even .small and marginal farmers, who otherwise can't afford to
purchase it, are not deprived of its benefits.
22. SCIENCE EXPRESS
22.1 The Rashtriya Vigyan Evam Prodyogiki Sanchar Parishad (RVPSP) has developed an
exhibition train ‘‘Science Express’’ in collaboration with Max Planck Society, Germany. This state
of the art exhibition, akin to their well know ground based ‘‘Science Tunnel’’, will take visitors
to a fascinating expedition into different issues of Modern Science through 12 thematic modules.
The presentation is through interactive plasma screens, TV monitors, PCs etc. The special train
would travel to about 57 selected destinations for 9 months. Colleges and schools in the districts
are being mobilized to visit the Science Express. The exhibition has a number of exciting activities
including the famous KIDZ LAB of BASF India, and on the spot competitions.
22.2 The Committee is of the view that the ‘Science Express’ programme of the
Department has shown encouraging results and should be further intensified and expanded
to the rural and backward areas of the country. There is need for better monitoring of the

viewers get more time while viewing.
23. GLOBAL WARMING
23.1 The phenomena of Global warming and climate change are emerging as one of the greatest
and most formidable challenges of the 21st century which are stated to have the potential of
pushing the world to the brink of a Catastrophe. Adaptation and mitigation are the two possible
ways and means identified to counter their effects. But these are not so easy solutions as they
appear to be. Science has to play a pivotal role in this direction. Department of Science and
Technology with its vast network of multi disciplinary laboratories and huge resource of competent
and expert man power has to take a lead role in galvanizing and dovetailing its activities and
resources to find viable solutions to provide relief to the nation and the world from this impending
calamity. It can address scientific issues relevant to atmosphere, geosphere, hydrosphere as well
as biosphere. It can assume the responsibility of standardizing all measurement of global change
with international traceability. The Committee feels that separate budgetary provisions for this
purpose should be made.
23.2 Ater considering the Demands for Grants of the Department of Science and
Technology assessing the progress of various important programmes and projects
administered by it, the Committee recommends that the budgetary allocation of Rs. 1780.00
crores under Demand No. 83 (Department of Science and Technology) as sought by the
Department for the year 2008-09 may be approved.

SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDATIONS
1. The Committee has been informed that the Department’s plan outlay of Rs. 1526
crores at the BE stage last year was reduced to Rs. 1270 crores at the RE stage. The
Department, however, was unable to spend even the reduced Grants during the last year.
The Committee takes serious note of the situation and recommends that the Department
should be more prompt and efficient in utilising the allocated funds. This acquires even
more importance because the rise in allocation this year, the Committee feels, is miniscule,
if put in the context of inflation and economic growth. At the same time the Committee
is of the opinion that, keeping in mind the responsibilities of the Department and the role
it is expected to play in development of science and technology, the Department should be
given an increase in allocation in consonance with its requirements. (Para 2.2)
2. The Committee welcomes the constitution of Expert Advisory Committees to monitor
and review the progress of its ongoing schemes and is of the opinion that such a step can
be helpful in prioritization and rationalisation of schemes. (Para 4.2)
3. The Secretary of the Department during the presentation made to the Committee
has informed that Science and Engineering Research Council (SERC) needs an increase in
allocation of about 25 per cent in order to fulfill its objectives. The Committee, keeping in
mind the huge array of responsibilities for promotion of research in newly emerging and
frontier areas of science and engineering including multidisciplinary fields; need for
encouraging young scientists to take up challenging R&D activities and imperatives to
promote basic and applied research in frontline areas of engineering and technology in
various academic and research institutions, etc., among many others, recommends that
sufficient budgetary support may be provided so that the programme could be pursued with
vigour. (Para 7.2)
4. The Committee has been informed that around 3000 research proposals are received
by the Department every year out of which 500-600 proposals are selected for funding. The
Committee is of the view that lack of fund should not be allowed to come in the way of
funding good and promising research proposals. (Para 7.3)
5. The success of Science can be gauged by the fact as to how far it has been able to
touch and ameliorate the life and lot of one and all. The Committee feels that going by this
yardstick a lot more is desired to be done. The Committee is of the opinion that science
should come out of the confines of laboratories to make its outreach to the common masses
and it needs to be done in a time bound manner or a sustained basis. This becomes all the
more imperative as India needs to shed its tag of a developing nation and acquire the
stature of a developed one, the sooner the better, and it is none other but science which
holds the magic stick to do wonders. DST being the nodal Ministry, the onus lies with it.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department of Science and Technology
should coordinate with all other scientific departments and institutions to move forward in
this direction and lay more and more emphasis on S&T programme for socio-economic
development. (Para 8.3)
6. The committee acknowledges the important role that TDP plays in translating lab-
scale research into technology mode but for which the benefit of science cannot be reaped.
The Committee, therefore, desires that Technology Development Programmes should be
14

15
further strengthened and intensified so that the advantages of new breakthroughs in the
field of science could be taken to the masses at the earliest and at an affordable cost.
(Para 9.4)
7. The Committee is also of the view that developing indigenous technology through
joint projects is also of utmost importance because without industry participation such
projects will not only become exorbitant but also lack the commercial dimension which is
very important for successful culmination of such projects. (Para 9.5)
8. The Committee is of the view that the mapping work should not suffer as a result
of inadequacy of funds, as it plays an important role in planning of resource utilization and
other schemes. (Para 10.3)
9. The Committee has been informed that DST plans to initiate five autonomous S&T
institutions in areas of glaciology, molecular materials, pre-competitive research institute
for computer sciences, etc., where India would require R&D capacities and need for National
initiatives for R&D in these areas have been felt. The Committee recommends that the
process of establishment of five autonomous Science and Technology institutions in different
fields be expedited so as to ensure that they become operational within the stipulated period
and become ready to meet the demands and expectations of these areas. The committee also
recommends that impact assessment study of other institutions on the lines of TIFAC &
NABL may also be undertaken so as to suitably restructure to derive maximum results out
of them. (Para 11.5)
10. The Committee recommends enhancing allocations for the project at the RE stage
because such a strategic project which has a catalytic effect on very important R&D and
technology development projects involving multiple agencies needs more funds for cutting-
edge research. (Para 12.3)
11. The Committee welcomes the initiative of the Department to upgrade the skills of
its scientists by conducting various training programmes which will certainly enable them
to meet contemporary standards and overcome any difficulties arising out of lack of
training. The Committee recommends that more funds may be provided by the Government
at RE stage so that some more training programmes may be added under this scheme.
(Para 13.5)
12. The Committee is of the view that in a country where poverty is rampant and
substantial part of population suffers from diseases, a continued effort in drug research is
required for providing cheaper medicines. Continued support to drug research programmes
should be provided to enable the scientists to find cheaper and effective drugs. The
Committee recommends that drug research programmes should focus on diseases which are
afflicting the large populace of our country. (Para 14.3)
13. The Committee reiterates it earlier recommendation that more efforts should be
made to make alternative system of medicines successfully fill in the gap in areas where
conventional cures are not available. The Committee felt that research in Traditional/
Alternative systems should focus on areas where conventional cures are either inadequate
or too costly. (Para 14.5)
14. The Committee welcomes the proposal to establish three major Institutes of Nano
Science and Technology and the introduction of PG Teaching Programmes (M.Sc./M.Tech.) in
Nano Science and Technology. The Committee is of the view that such proactive steps are
required for creating a pool of scientists to cater to the needs of this unfolding research
frontier which holds immense potential for the future. (Para 15.4)

16
15. The Committee appreciates the scheme and is of the view that the above programme
is a step taken in right direction and more such programmes are required to initiate and
retain students in the field of science. The Committee feels that funds should not be
allowed to be an obstacle as the future of science and of the country rests on such small
beginnings which will have crucial effects on the future. (Para 16.3)
16. The Committee feels that the geographical reach of SHE should also be extended to
distant parts of the country like Ladakh and the North-East and other backward States. The
Committee has also been informed that the Department was unable to implement the 'SHE'
scheme because it required consultation and approval of several departments. The
Committee recommends that the Department expedite the process of consultation along
with other Departments for speedy execution of proposals. Beside this the Committee also
recommends that a special effort should be made to increase the reach of the programmes
to students who are not as advantaged as in the Metros but are equally deserving and this
should specially take into consideration girl students who are unable to take advantage of
opportunities. (Para 16.4)
17. In the light of the serious crunch in availability of quality scientists, schemes like
INSPIRE along with other such schemes need constant focus and attention. Scheme for
Early Attracting of Talents for Science (SEATS) and Assured Opportunity for Research
Careers (AORC) in the age group of 22-32 years for 5 years doctoral research backed by
an assured research career opportunity scheme for a another period of five years after their
Ph.D. in sciences are well-thought schemes which if properly implemented have the
potential to meet the intended targets and the Committee, therefore, feels that these
schemes should be given the required attention. (Para 17.4)
18. The Committee is of the view that the Department should prioritize its activities and
focus on its core competencies rather than spreading its resources too thin. The top-most
priority should be given to tapping young talent through various monetary and motivational
schemes. Stress should be laid on ‘catching them young’. (Para 17.5)
19. The Committee is of the opinion that a project for development of low cost filters
for domestic purposes should be given top-most priority as millions of households in this
country, for want of affordable filters, suffer from waterborne diseases. Integrating effective
technologies to purify drinking water supplied by civic authorities is yet another challenge
to be taken by the Department in larger interest. The Committee would also like the
Department to enter into partnership with Industry so as to make such products
commercial and popular. (Para 18.4)
20. The Committee is also of the opinion that such water treatment technology should
be made available in large scale catering to the needs at community level and arsenic,
fluoride, iron and other hazardous minerals should be removed before it reaches
households. The Committee is of the further view that there is an urgent need to develop
models which would be low cost, low power consuming and which can benefit people of
different parts of the country afflicted by the problem. (Para 18.5)
21. The Committee is of the opinion that an innovation infrastructure to link knowledge
products to the generation of wealth is of immense importance in knowledge economy. Rich
fruits of research should also be commercially viable to sustain themselves and encourage
further research. Innovation clusters benefiting the academy and industrial sectors under
an effective public-private partnership model is the need of the hour for future successes
of research initiatives. (Para 19.30)

17
22. The convergence of technology and security issues is indicative of the highly
technological world we are living in. Technology not only determines how we live our lives
but also how we protect ourselves from negative forces determined to destroy our social and
economic fabric. It is here that the Committee feels that technology has an important role
to play in intelligence gathering as well as monitoring internal security situation and it
urges that the Department should do all that is possible to achieve breakthroughs in
security technology in a time bound manner so that we could be in a position to effectively
tackle the threats posed to our internal security and improve our intelligence gathering
capabilities. (Para 20.3)
23. The Committee welcomes the symbiotic research initiative taken by the Department
along with Department of Atomic Energy (DAE). Identification of areas where an effective
partnership of the two departments can bring about an effective capacity building in the
university and academic sector for building mega faculties for basic research is of utmost
importance as it is a known fact that without progress in basic science, technological
progress cannot sustain itself for very long. (Para 21.4)
24. The Committee has been informed that the Department has developed a soil-testing
kit, which costs Rs. 3000 per unit. The Committee would like the Department to popularise
the kit among farmers and rope in Industry to promote the product. The Committee also
recommends that the Department should coordinate with the Ministry of Agriculture to
promote its uses among the farmers. It also recommends that at least one soil testing kit
be made available free of cost at the Panchayat or Village level so that even small and
marginal farmers, who otherwise can't afford to purchase it, are not deprived of its benefits.
(Para 21.5)
25. The Committee is of the view that the ‘Science Express’ programme of the
Department has shown encouraging results and should be further intensified and expanded
to the rural and backward areas of the country. There is need for better monitoring of the
programme for crowd management and more such expresses should be introduced so that
viewers get more time while viewing. (Para 22.2)
26. After considering the Demands for Grants of the Department of Science and
Technology assessing the progress of various important programmes and projects
administered by it, the Committee recommends that the budgetary allocation of Rs. 1780.00
crores under Demand No. 83 (Department of Science and Technology) as sought by the
Department for the year 2008-09 may be approved. (Para 23.2)

deals with the detailed Demands for Grants (2008-09) of the Department of Scientific and

2. In the meeting of the Committee held on the 25th March, 2008, the Secretary and other
Officers of the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research gave an overview of the various
activities of the Department and the Members sought clarifications on various aspects of the
performance of the Department to enable it to scrutinise the Demands for Grants.
