13 HEALTH HAZARD OF URANIUM MINES 
13.1 The Committee also raised th e issue of the health hazard posed due to the existing 
mining and milling plants of Uranium ore, wh ich has become a cause of major concern 
for the local population and enquired about the steps that have  been taken by the 
department in this regard. The Committee also pointed out a specific instance of Jajugada 
in the Singhbhum district wher e there have been instances of health problems for the 
local community ranging from miscarriage to children born with physical and mental 
deformities. The department clarified that as the operations of Uranium Corporation of 

 
India Limited(UCIL) are carried out under strict surveillance of Atomic Energy 
Regulatory Board, State Pollution Control Board and Director-g eneral of Mines 
Safety(DGMS), there is no adverse effect due to the mining of uranium ore and the same 
has been confirmed by the various studies carried out by the experts. Further, local Health 
Physics Units of the Bhabha Atomic Resear ch Centre present in the locality are 
monitoring the activity on day to  day basis to ensure the sa fety aspect. The department 
also pointed out that on the basis of medical reports it has been confirmed that most of 
the diseases in the areas n ear the mines are due to malnutrition, malaria and unhygienic 
living conditions rather than the side-effect of radiation. 
13.2 The Committee while acknowledging the need of the department to increase 
its Uranium sources through development of  new mines, would like to stress upon 
the importance of avoiding the resulting health hazards and maintaining the ecology 
and environment of the areas near the mines.  The Committee is also aware that in 
some regions of the country Uranium pros pecting has led to public unrest due to 
resulting health hazards and displacement of people. The Committ ee feels that the 
department should take preventive steps to ensure that there is  no adverse effect 
due to the mining operations. Before mining operation starts the department should 
make consistent efforts for winning over th e confidence of public by making aware 
of the factual information to all stakeholde rs of the project through extensive public 
awareness programmes.  The department sh ould also ensure proper compensation 
for the displaced people to avoid public di scontentment at a later stage and also 
undertake welfare measure programmes in th e entire area by opening schools, 
hospitals, etc.

energy being dismal, the future projections, i.e., 6-7 per cent by 2020 and 10 per cent 
by 2032 are also not very encouraging.  Th e Committee is conscious that the Deptt. 
is also concerned about it.  However, it recommends that the Deptt. must devise 
some way out to enhance the power generation capacity. 
14.8 The Committee is of the view that th e Department of Atomic Energy through 
its various research and development activities  is striving very hard against all odds 
to uplift the standard of living in the count ry.  The Committee is happy to note that 
starting from a very modest  beginning the Deptt. has brought the country on the 
verge of becoming an export  oriented country.  Keeping in view the excellent work 
that the Department has done, the kind of competence it has exhibited and the kind 

 
of core and critical programmes it has envisaged for the future, the Committee 
strongly recommends that the Department  of Atomic Energy should be properly 
and adequately funded and any kind of reduction in outlay at R.E. stage should be 
strictly avoided.

REPORT 
The primary endeavour of the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research 
(DSIR) is to encourage indus try to increase their share in  country’s R&D expenditure, 
support a larger cross section of small and medium industrial units to develop state-of-the 
art globally competitive technologies of high commercial potential, catalyze faster 
commercialization of lab-scale R&D, enhan ce the share of technol ogy intensive exports 
in overall exports, strengthen industrial consultancy & technology management 
capabilities and establish user friendly info rmation network to facilitate scientific & 
industrial research in  the country. The Department also  acts as an administrative link 
between the Government of India and the CSIR society. 
1.2.  The mandate of DSIR includes promoti on of industrial research for indigenous 
technology promotion, development, utilizatio n and transfer. The allocation of business 
of the Department is as under:  
i. All matters concerning the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research;  
ii. All matters relating to National Research Development Corporation;  
iii. All matters relating to Central Electronics Limited; 
iv.  Registration and Recognition of R&D Units; 
v. Matters relating to UNCTAD and WIPO; 
vi.  National Register for Foreign Collaborations; and 
vii. Matters relating to creation of pool  for temporary placement of Indian 
Scientists and Technologists.  

2. ORGANISATIONAL SETUP 
2.1. The DSIR has two autonomous organiza tions viz Council of Scientific and 
Industrial Research (CSIR) and Consultanc y Development Centre (CDC) and two public 
sector undertakings viz. National Research Developm ent Corporation (NRDC) and 
Central Electronics Limited (CEL). The De partment also provide s institutional host 
facilities to Asia Pacific Centre for Transfer of Technology (APCTT).  
3. MECHANISM TO MONITOR AND REVIEW THE ONGOING SCHEMES  
3.1 The Committee has been informed th at DSIR has developed monitoring and 
reviewing mechanisms both at external and inter-departmental levels. At the external 
level the department has been reviewing the progress of on-going schemes by involving 
an external agency or outside experts at th e beginning of every five year plan. At the 
beginning of XIth five year plan, DSIR entrusted a study to Indian Institute of  
Management, Bangalore to assess the impact of DSIR programmes in the Xth five year 
plan. Besides this, each scheme in the depa rtment has an inter-departmental Technical 
Advisory Committee which reviews the progr ess of on-going projects and recommends 
for new projects and programmes. The propos als for budgetary support are formulated 
keeping in view the requirement of funds under ongoing as well as new proposals.  
3.2 In the CSIR has refocused and repositio ned its R&D activities (of Eleventh Five 
Year Plan) responding to the Government dire ctions/ policy changes. For the purpose, 
activities of CSIR laboratori es have been regrouped in si x clusters viz. Biological 
Sciences, Chemical Sciences, Engineering Sciences, Physical Sciences, Information 
Sciences, and CSIR-800. The monitoring and review of the ongoing schemes/projects at 
CSIR is being carried out through: Internal Monitoring; and External Monitoring. Internal 
Monitoring is done at (i) Task Force level, ( ii) Cluster level, and (iii) Council of CSIR 
Clusters level. External Monitoring is done through (i ) Research Council of the 
respective CSIR laboratories/institutes, and (ii) Sectoral Monitoring Committee involving 
peers from Academia, Industrial Enterprises and other Technical Agencies. 
4. ELEVENTH  FIVE  YEAR  PLAN OUTLAY AND PROPOSALS 
4.1 The Committee has been informed that  the total budgetary allocation for the 
Department for Eleventh Five Year Plan  is Rs. 9000.00 crores. The various schemes 
undertaken by the Department and its constituents during the Five Year Plan are:  
(a) Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) schemes  
DSIR is implementing programmes towa rds technology promotion, development 
and utilization through Tec hnology Promotion, Developmen t and Utilization (TPDU) 
programmes. The components include Tech nology Development and Demonstration 
Programme (TDDP); Technopreneur Promo tion Programme (TePP); Technological 
Empowerment of Women and Implementation of Flagship Programmes. 
(b) Consultancy Development Centre (CDC)  
Several new programmes and schemes rela ting to development and promotion of 
consultancy profession have been planned. Th ese include creating a large pool of human 
resource for the consulting profession, intr oducing schemes for fellowship and internship 
for young professionals to opt consulting as a career option, launching scheme for 
capacity building of client or ganizations including setting up of Novel Assessment Units 
for Training, Innovation, Capacity Augm entation and Learning (NAUTICALs) in 
research institutions, including CSIR.  
(c) Central Electronics Limited (CEL)  
The capacity enhancement to manufactur e phased control modules (PCM) from 
30,000-40,000 to 70,000 per annum and creating ma nufacturing and test facilities for 
piezo generator will be implemented dur ing the plan period. The proposals for the 
development of dye-sensitized so lar cells and enhancing the e fficiency of the solar cells 

shall be taken up. The CEL also plans to expand PV manufacturing capacity to 100 MW 
in two phases viz. 25 MW by the year 2012 and then up to 100 MW.  
(d) National Research Development Corporation (NRDC)  
 The main objective of  NRDC is to commercialize the R& D results of publicly 
funded R& D institutions as well as to promote the growth of the indigenous technology. 
 (e) Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR )  
CSIR is an autonomous orga nization of the Department and its schemes includes   
the National Laboratories, Na tional S&T Human Resource De velopment, Intellectual 
Property & Technology Mana gement, R&D Management Support, New Millennium 
Indian Technology Leadership Initiative, and Setting up Institute of Translational 
Research . 
4.2 The Committee has been informed that CSIR  during Xth  plan operated six 
schemes of which five, are continuing into XI Plan as well and the Infrastructure 
Refurbishing & Renovation (IRR) scheme has been discontinued in the X
th  Plan. Sixteen 
network projects under National Laboratory sche me were permitted to spillover into the 
XIth Plan. Thirteen projects have been completed while three projects are still continuing. 
The reason for spillover into XIth Plan is late  start of these projec ts as Standing Finance 
Committee (SFC) and Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) approvals took time. 
4.3 The Committee appreciates the achievemen ts made so far by the Department 
during the X th Five  Year Plan and hopes that the Department will strive towards 
continuing and strengthening its progra mme to support the small and medium 
industrial units to develop cutting edge tech nologies of high co mmercial value and  
intensify exports and at the same time de veloping technologies for the use of the 
common man. However, the Committee takes note of the fact that although six 
schemes initially operated by CSIR five are now continuing into XI th plan, while 
Infrastructure Refurbishing & Renovation (I RR) scheme has been discontinued in 
the XI th plan.  The Committee however noticed no significant reasons have been 
provided by DSIR for discontinuance of IRR Scheme.  Moreover sixteen network 
projects under National Laboratory scheme were permitted to spillover into the XIth 
plan.  The reasons quoted for such spillover is the late start of these projects as 
Standing Finance Committee (SFC) and Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) 
approvals took time.     
4.4 The Committee feels that non agreeability between Standing Finance 
Committee and Expenditure Finance Committee might have led to the late approval 
of sixteen network projects  under NLS for which these projects have been spilled 
over to XI
th  plan leading to delay in project implementation.  Committee apprehend 
that  disagreeability between SFC and EFC might have taken place due to the fact 
that there might be some major changes in  the project content in comparison to 
initial proposal.  The Committee therefore fe els that the revised cost estimates in 
respect of every scientific project should be made in such a manner that escalation 
in the cost of projects due to prevailing in flation at the revised estimate stage should 
not be exceeded more than 20 percent of the original cost estimate.  As per the 
opinion of the  Committee this can be achieved if there is no major changes 
proposed in the content of the project at  R.E. level, then only disagreeability 
between SFC and EFC could be avoided a nd project approvability may be granted 
without any delay. 
 

5. BUDGETARY ALLOCATION  
5.1. The Budgetary Estimates of the Department  of Scientific and Industrial Research 
for the year 2010-2011 is Rs. 2988.00 crores  with a Plan component of                    
Rs.1600.00 crores and Non-Plan compone nt of Rs.1388.00 crores as compared to a                          
B.E. allocation of Rs.2691.00 crores and R.E. allocation of Rs.2697.75 crores for the year 
2009-2010. 
5.2 The Committee enquired as to whether the funds allocated were sufficient to carry 
out the activities of the Depa rtment. In reply, the department stated that the projected 
demand of the department for 2010-2011 was Rs. 4150.98 crore with a component of                             
Rs. 2615.00 crore for Plan and Rs. 1535.98 crore for Non-plan allocation. However, the 
department has been allotted Rs . 2988.00 crore only, with Rs.1600.00 crore for Plan and                         
Rs. 1388.00 crore for Non-Plan allo cation. The department stated  that while this will be 
sufficient, in a limited way, to support ongo ing activities under various schemes in the 
Eleventh Five Year Plan, the non-plan compon ent might be constrained due to low level 
of funding against increased requirem ent on account of Sixth Pay Commission 
recommendations. Apart from that there is a continuous increase in pensionary liability 
due to large number of pensioners in CSIR . The maintenance cost of infrastructure 
created during Xth Plan also needs additiona l Non-Plan budgetary support. The reduced 
Plan allocation may affect the  ambitious me ga projects of the C ouncil of Scientific & 
Industrial Research such as ‘Open Source Drug Discovery’ which has just been initiated, 
the ‘Solar Mission’, ‘Energy Efficiency Mi ssion’, ‘Micromachines & Robotics’, and the 
‘CSIR-800’ will also be affected under th e respective R&D domains of ‘Affordable 
Healthcare’, ‘Sustainable Energy’, ‘Chemistry & Environment and Smart & Functional 
Materials’, ‘Engineering Structures and Design & Electronics’, and ‘Societal Mission’.  
5.3 In view of the shortfall th e other schemes/projects that  are likely to be affected 
under the following broad heads include:  
TPDU:Technology Development an d Demonstration Programme, 
Technopreneur Promotion Programme.  
CDC:   Studies on Science & Technology Proposals for XII five year plan.  
NRDC: Funding for promoting devel opment of new generation products, 
Promotion of Export of Technol ogy, Basic Engineering Design 
Packages and Technology Development Program for Priority Projects.  
CEL: Development of Dye-sensitized Solar Cells  
The Department also informed that th e additional funds would be required under 
Technology Development and Demonstration Programme (TPDU), Central Electronics 
Limited(CEL) and National Lab schemes of CSIR for which demand would be made at 
RE stage. For CDC, the Department will re-p rioritize allocation within various heads to 
initiate work and complete the activiti es in the following year. For NRDC, the 
Department will take important activities by increasing its comm ercial operations and 
defer some of the planned activities to next year. For CEL, the Department will request 
for additional funds at R.E. stage and de fer project on developm ent of Dye-sensitized 
Solar Cells to next year.  
5.4 The Department also informed  that at the beginning of XI
th F i v e  Y e a r  P l a n ,  
around 225 projects under National Laboratories scheme were formulated for CSIR. 
However due to reduced allocation, Depart ment has prioritized  its projects for 
implementation. As a first priority 91 projects have been taken up for implementation 
during the plan period. The remaining project s would be taken up for implementation as 
and when sufficient funds are made available to the Department. 
5.5 The Committee notes with serious co ncern that there has been a drastic 
reduction in the Plan allocation for the department, amounting to Rs.1015.00 crores.   

Moreover the allocation for DSIR during 2009-10 was slashed from Rs. 58.50 crore 
at BE stage to Rs. 31.31 crore at RE stage.  Due to this reduction, the Department 
will need to re-prioritize allocation within  various heads to initiate work and will 
even have to defer some of the activities planned for that year to next year due to 
paucity of funds.  
5.6 The Committee also notes with seri ous concern the significant difference 
between the demand projected by the De partment and the amount actually 
allocated. The Committee is of the opinion th at investment in scientific research is a 
step towards ensuring the development of the country. Therefore at least the 
scientific Departments  should not be depriv ed of funds as it would adversely affect 
research and development which is crucial for the development of the nation. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that the well thought out projected demand of 
scientific departments should be ho noured and accepted by the Planning 
Commission, specially in view of the fact that scientific research is a capital intensive 
field. 
5.7 The  Committee observes that though the Department has been making an 
outstanding contribution towards the res earch and development in the various 
sectors of science & technol ogy and has played a pivotal ro le in the progress of the 
country, yet the acknowledgement of its acti vities has been  utterly disappointing  
and  its activities are not popular as co mpared to those of the other scientific 
departments. The Committee feels that this  is one of the root causes for the 
reduction of the budgetary allocation by  the Planning Commission. The Committee 
therefore recommends that the Department should have a comprehensive plan and 
a separate budget for populariz ing its technologies and shou ld double its efforts to 
communicate its activities and market it s products to the Government and the 
private sector both through audio-visual an d print media in a more effective way.  
In this direction the initiative of Department to have a CSIR logo on all the products 
using CSIR technology should be vigor ously pursued. The Planning Commission 
should also on its part encourage the sc ientific departments with adequate fund 
allocation in keeping with their proposed allocations so that most of the programme 
may not be spilled over to the future years and could be completed within the 
targeted time frame. 
6. PROGRAMMES OF THE DEPART MENT OF SCIENTIFIC AND 
INDUSTRIAL RESEARCH 
6.1 Technology Promotion, Development and Utilisation (TPDU) Programme 
The Department of Scientific and Indus trial Research operates a plan scheme 
called the ‘Technology Promotion, Developm ent and Utilization(TPDU) Programme’. 
The specific components of the scheme are: 
 Industrial R&D Promotion Programme; 
 Technology Development and Demonstration Programme; 
 Technopreneur Promotion Programme; 
 Technology Management Programme; 
 International Technology Transfer Programme;  
 Consultancy Promotion Programme; 
 Technology Information Facilitation Programme; 
 Technology Development and Utilization Programme for Women; 
 IT& e-Goverance; and 
 Asian and Pacific Centre for Transfer of Technology  

6.2 The details of the specific compon ents of the ‘Technology Promotion, 
Development and Utilization (TPDU) Programme scheme are as under : 
6.2.1 Industrial R&D Promotion Programme 
DSIR is the nodal Department for granti ng recognition to in-house Research and 
Development centres. The programme deals with  all activities relating to recognition of 
in-house R&D units in industry and non-commer cial Scientific and Industrial Research 
Organisations, fiscal incentives and other m echanisms and initiatives towards supporting 
and encouraging R&D efforts of industry. In centives and support measures provided 
under the scheme contribute a great deal in enhancing the R&D expenditure by 
recognized in-house R&D units of industry. 
6.2.2 Technology Development and Demonstration Programme  
 The programme aims at catalyzing and supporting activities relating to technology 
absorption, adaptation and demonstration including capital goods development, involving 
industry and R&D organizations . Under the scheme, projects for absorption and                              
up-gradation of imported technology as well  as development and demonstration of new 
and improved technologies are supported.  While DSIR support has been catalytic and 
partial, bulk of the financia l contribution in such projects have been from the industry. 
These projects cover products and processes in various important industries such as 
metallurgy, electrical, electronics, instrumentation, mechanical engineering, earth moving 
and industrial machinery, chemicals and explosives.  
6.2.3 Technopreneur Promotion Programme  
The programme aims to tap the vast innova tive potential of the citizens of India. 
The activities under TePP include providing fina ncial support to individual innovators 
having original ideas and convert them into working models, prototypes, etc.  
6.2.4 Technology Management Programme 
The programme aims to enhance knowledge and skills in the efficient 
management and transfer of technology. It s activities effectiv ely supplement other 
programmes/activities of the Department in th e attainment of technological excellence. 
Specific programmes have been targeted towards enhancing technology management 
capability in industry, R&D institutions, acad emic institutes and other establishments. 
This is helping the promotion and eff ective utilization of emerging technology 
management methodologies, and in bringing about better indust ry-institute inter-linkages 
through networking of industrial units with different academ ic institutions and State 
bodies in various States.   
6.2.5 International Technology Transfer Programme 
The Programme aims to promote intern ational technology transfer and trade 
including exports of technologies, projects, services and hi-tech products. A variety of 
activities have been undertaken under the programme to cata lyze technology transfer and 
trade, involving Indian industries, R&D es tablishments, institutions and consultancy 
organisations. These have ranged from Reports, Compendiums and Newsletters on 
technology export potential, Workshops a nd Awareness-cum-Training Programmes, 
Technology Exhibitions, etc.  
6.2.6 Consultancy Promotion Programme 
The main objective of Consultancy Prom otion Programme is to promote and 
strengthen consultancy capabilities for domestic use and export requirements. It also aims 
to develop sector specific consultancy capabilities and provide door step consultancy 
services to Small and Medium Enterprises.   
6.2.7 Technology Information Facilitation Programme 
Technology Information Facilitation Pr ogramme has been included under the 
TPDU Programmes to provide a strong back up support of information services.  The 

projects under TIFP aim at developing appropr iate indigenous information capacities to 
support R&D activities, production of local content and capture of indigenous knowledge 
base, promotion of information and knowledge  networking thus f acilitating flow and 
sharing of information resources.

and accountability.

The programme promotes in ternational cooper ation in the areas of industrial

6.3  On being enquired about the allocat ion to Technology Promotion, Development 
and Utilisation (TPDU)Programme, which in  2009-2010 stood at Rs. 37.50 crores at  
B.E. stage and was decreased to Rs 12.50 crores at R.E. stages and has b een increased to                             
Rs. 32.00 crores in B.E. 2010-2011. The department clarified that the TPDU allocation in 
2009-2010 was drastically cut at the RE stage because of meager spending till October, 
2009 but thereafter, activities have picked up and department could have spent higher 
amounts, if the funds were available. Furthe r, during 2010-2011 in vi ew of initiation and 
revision of some TPDU programmes, increased allocation is required.  
6.4 The Department was successful in achievi ng the physical targets of X five year 
plan. However, there were shortfalls in achieving the financial targets under the TPDU 
Programme. While the X Plan outlay for TPDU Programme was Rs. 99.00 crore, the 
actual expenditure was Rs. 67.74 crore. One r eason for this has been dearth of good 
proposals, in spite of publicity through press, media and promotional workshops. Another 
reason has been non-receipt of u tilization certificates from th e beneficiaries in the first 
half of the financial year, in spite of rigorous follow-up, thereby leading to slashing of the 
budget at the RE stage. 
6.5 The Committee notes with serious concern that the TPDU allocation for the             
2009-2010 was drastically reduced to Rs. 12.50 cro res at the R.E. stage, which is less 
than half of the initial allocation of  Rs.37.50 crores at the B.E. stage, as the 
Department was unable to ensure proper ut ilisation of the funds allocated till 
October, 2009.   
6.6 The Committee has also noticed that wh ile the department was successful in 
achieving the physical targets of Xth five year plan, however there were shortfalls in 
achieving the financial targets under th e TPDU Programme for which initially 
under Xth plan Rs. 99.00 crore was allocated out of which only Rs. 67.74 crore was 
spent and Rs. 31.26 crore remain unspent.  The reason quoted by DSIR for such 
shortfall in actual expenditure under TPDU programme was inadequate publicity of 
the programme through printed and tale media, dearth of good proposals received 
for the programme and non-receip t of utilization certificat es from the beneficiaries 
of the  programme in spite of rigorous follow-up.  By going through the entire 
explanation given by the department about TPDU programme, the committee feels 

that the monitoring of the programme is no t at all satisfactory on the part of the 
department and that is why the utilization certificate could not have been obtained 
from the beneficiaries in spite of the  strict follow up of TPDP.  The Committee 
therefore is of the opinion that the monito ring mechanism of the projects adopted 
by the department contains deficiencies at every stage which needs to be strengthen   
and spilling over of projects to future plan  period should be avoided as far as 
possible so that strategic projects could be completed within  a reasonable time 
frame. The Committee feels that it is a serious lacunae on the part of the 
Department as regards the proper manage ment and utilization of funds allocated 
for the TPDU.  
6.7 The Committee feels  that the various  programmes and activities under the 
TPDU are essential for the nation as it promotes industrial research & development, 
commercialization and export of indigenous technologies, acquisition of cutting edge 
technologies from abroad, promotion of co nsultancy capabilities and  also ensures 
participation of both public and private sectors in technology development efforts. 
Therefore the Committee strongly recomm ends that the Department should 
formulate a comprehensive plan and take follow-up measures to overcome 
procedural problems such as non-receipt of utilization cert ificates from the 
beneficiaries, for optimal utilization of  funds for the scheme in future. The 
Department should also ensure proper pub licity of the TPDU schemes through the 
print and audio-visual media to draw more proposals for the schemes. 
GLOBAL KNOWLEDGE PARTNERSHIP  
6.8 The Commitee has been informed th at Under the International Technology 
Transfer Programme, the ‘Global Knowledge  Partnerships’ of the Department for 
promotion of Technology Transfer at an in ternational level is  going on with four 
countries viz. Germany, Japan, France and USA. The programme requires equal 
investments by the partners. Refering to a particular programme called the ‘Green 
Chemistry’ the Committee was informed that the National Chemical Laboratory has tied 
up with the Max Planck Group, Germany to  reduce toxic by-pro ducts of cemical 
industries, while in another partnership with  Japan a combination of cancer drugs in low 
concentration is being experimented upon to reduce the toxicity of the cancer drugs. 
6.9 The  Committee is of the opinion that  such ‘Global Knowledge Partnerships’ 
are the need of the hour, where both the co nstituent partners stand to benefit from 
each others competence. Such programmes besides building up the confidence of 
our researchers would also be economically beneficial for the country as the 
investments costs of the research programme s are shared by both the partnering 
countries. The Committee the refore recommends that such programmes should be 
further intensified with more partnerships  particularly with South East Asian 
Countries  like Japan, Korea, China etc.  apart from other  scientifically advanced 
countries of Europe and strengthened with more funds allocation. 
6.10 The Committee is glad to learn that CSIR had planned two mega projects 
and specific programmes in R&D domain su ch as Chemistry and Environment and 
Smart and Functional Materials and Engineering Structures/Design and 
Electronics.  Within these programmes the green Chemistry mission  as mentioned 
in    para 6.7 above may be  encouraged in view of the global warming and climate 
changes.   The Committee feels that for de veloping green chemistry technology in 
addition to collaboration with Max planck Group, Germany, collaboration with 
America, France and Britain should also be  encouraged  in the field so that the 
global leaders in the technology could co ntribute to their maximum in developing 
the green chemistry in the country in the wake of persistent climate change

 The  Autonomous institutions include the Council of Scie ntific & Industrial 
Research(CSIR) and the Consultancy Development Centre(CDC).

The  CSIR is implementing six schemes, which are as follows: 
i) National Laboratories, 
ii) National S&T Human Resource Development 
iii) Intellectual Property & Technology Management, 
iv) R&D Management Support, 
v) New Millennium Indian Technology Leadership Initiative, and

7.2 National Laboratories 
 The National Laboratories Scheme is operated through 37 National Laboratories 
and 38 field Centres. During the 11th Plan the research programmes/projects/activities  of 
the laboratories have been categorized into  the following major socio-economic sectors 
viz. Aerospace Science & Engineering; Agro, Food Processing & Nutrition Technology; 
Biology& Biotechnology; Chem ical Science & Technology; Earth System Science; 
Ecology & Environment; Sustainable Energy; El ectronics, Photonics & Instrumentation; 
Engineering Materials, Mining/Mineral s& Manufacturing Technology; Affordable 
Healthcare; Housing, Road &Construction; Information Technology; Resources & 
Products; Leather; Meteorology; Rural Development and Water Resources & 
Technology. The CSIR is also striving towards creating a Sc ientists’ Pool with the  
objective of promoting and creating a p ool of qualified, highly specialized 
scientists/engineers and technologists in R&D in all disciplines of S&T in the country. 
7.3     The Department has informed the Committee that for National Laboratories the 
allocation has been increased from Rs.1807.00 crores at B.E. in 2009-2010 to                       
Rs. 1877.30 crores in R.E. 2009-2010 and then again increased to Rs.2120.00 crores in              
B.E. 2010-2011. Explaining the reasons for the increase the department explained that 
under the Plan allocation of the National Laboratories Scheme, out of 94 priority projects 
89 projects were ongoing and two new projects were initiated during 2009-2010. 
Majority of them have a projection of enhanced activitie s in the fourth year of the              
XIth Five year Plan. In  addition, some other priority pr ojects have been planned to be 
initiated during 2010-2011. Under Non Plan, a dditional funds are required for meeting 
the requirement of enhanced salary and pension budget due to implementation of Sixth 
Pay Commission recommendations.  
7.4 The Committee appreciates the fact th at under the XIth Five Year Plan 
allocation of the National Laboratories  Scheme, 89 projects out of 94 sanctioned 
priority projects have been started a nd two new projects were initiated during  
2009-2010. The Committee hopes that the enha nced activities for the priority 
projects which have been projected during th e fourth year of the XIth Five year 
Plan would be completed and the two ne w projects would be initiated as per 
schedule.  
7.5 The Committee also enquired as to wh ether the Department was exploring the 
issue of opening National Laboratories in the st ates where there are no such laboratories, 
specially in the state of Bi har and in Andhra Pradesh. The Department stated that the 
proposal of opening a laboratory has been di scussed in the recently held State Council 
meeting and there are also proposals for the state of Sikkim and Chattisgarh which lack 
such laboratories. Requirement of land is al so being considered for setting up a Marine 
Research Laboratory in Vishakhapatnam. 
 

7.6 The Committee recommends that the ex pansion of National Laboratories 
should be extended to all the states of the country, with at least one laboratory in 
each state so that there is equitable scie ntific progress in each state. The Committee 
also desires that comprehensive plans for setting of the National Laboratory  in 
states which lack such facility may be forwarded to the state governments, for 
preferential allotment of land.    
7.7 The Committee is of the view that th e investment in science can only be 
fruitful in case its benefi ts reaches the common man. Pr esently, the Committee feels 
that though the National Laboratories are doing a lot of ingenious work as regards  
research and development in various scientific spheres  but most of its achievements 
are not reaching the common man. In fact the Committee feels that the Department 
of Scientific and Industrial Research can justify an increase in the Budgetary 
allocation only if substantial benefits reach the common man. The Committee 
therefore recommends that the department  should focus towards transfer of 
technologies from the National Laboratories to the society particularly strategic 
areas to give benefit to the user.   
7.8 ‘CSIR-800’Programme 
The Committee has been informed that a new programme namely,                         
‘CSIR-800’has been started by the department  with the mission of increasing the daily 
per capita income by Rs. 15.00 of 800 million peopl e of India said to be subsisting in the 
bottom half of the pyramid.  The focus areas are ‘affordable health’, ‘sustainable energy’, 
‘waste to wealth’, ‘potable water’, low-co st housing’, and ‘empowering masses’, In this 
new endeavour, CSIR has launched ‘Soleckshaw ’, an optimally designed, pedal-operated 
motor-assisted, zero carbon emission urban transpor t vehicle. It is expected to have four 
major societal effects viz. conservation of  natural petroleum resources, zero pollution , 
increased self-employment of  the poor, enha ncing the dignity of of human labour and 
cutting down the drudgery and exhaustion of pedaling traditional rickshaws. 
7.9 The Committee is of the opinion that since its inception, CSIR has played a 
very crucial role in the development of industrial technologies and research and 
development in various scientific areas. A time has come when it should increase its 
societal role and generate technologies fo r the common and deprived masses. In this 
direction the Department has taken a pro- active step towards facilitating a  
socialistic, yet commercially viable business model linked to the economic prosperity 
of a large and deprived masses throug h its CSIR-800 programme. The Committee 
therefore recommends that such progra mmes should be pursued vigorously and 
adequately funded so that the objectives of the programme are attained. 
7.10 Open Source Drug Discovery (OSDD) Programme 
 The Committee has been  informed that CSIR has conceptualized and launched an 
‘Open Source Drug Discovery (OSDD) progra mme’ during XI Five Year Plan, with a 
vision to provide affordable healthcare to the developing world. Initially focused at 
Tuberculosis, this global initi ative is a CSIR led ‘Team India’ consortium based on the 
principles of ‘Collaborate, Share and Di scover’. Open to global participation, OSDD 
programme represents a viable alternative m odel of drug discovery for neglected tropical 
infectious diseases, as it enables expansion of resources by allowing open access to the 
participants on one hand and incentivises contribution to the cooperative efforts on the 
other hand.  Presently there are more th an 2500 contributors, the best minds can 
collaborate and collectively endeavour to so lve the complex problems associated with 
discovering novel therapies for neglected tropi cal diseases like Malaria, Tuberculosis, 
Leishmaniasis, etc.  

7.11 The Committee is aware that even in this age of medical advancement, there 
are a lot of fatalities in our country due to common tropical diseases like Malaria, 
Tuberculosis etc. due to absence of pr oper medication. The Committee therefore 
feels that the department should inve st substantially in the research and 
development and devise innovative method s for inventing new drugs. In this 
direction, the ‘Open drug Discovery Programme’ is an innovative method wherein  
the researchers can collectively utilize thei r knowledge base for the discovery of a 
drugs. This will also bring down the cost involved in the research and development 
process. The Committee therefore strongly recommends that the Department should 
give adequate budgetary support to this innovative programme.   
8. INITIATIVES BY THE  DEPARTMENT 
8.1  Mega Project on Solar Energy 
The Committee desired to know the contri bution made by the Department in the 
field of Solar energy. The Department has stat ed that it has initiated a ‘Mega Project on 
Solar Energy’ as Solar Energy, both thr ough Photovoltaics (PV) and Solar Thermal 
routes present tremendous opportunity for Indi a.  CSIR had done pioneering work in this 
area during the 1970s but since then the focu s shifted due to absence of appropriate 
policies of the Government. The Department through its P ublic Sector Undertaking, 
namely, Central Electronics Limited, has made  immense contributions in the field of 
Solar Photovoltaics. CSIR is presently initi ating a mega project on Solar Energy  in 
partnership with Network Institute for Sustai nable Energy (NISE) and Research Institute 
of Sustainable Energy (RISE) under Jawahar Lal Nehru Solar Mission.  
8.2 The Committee is of the opinion that I ndia being a tropical country has a lot 
of potential in the field of solar ener gy and appreciates the initiative of the 
Department in starting the Mega Project fo r large scale utilization of solar energy 
The Committee feels that the Department  should explore the possibilities of 
exploiting more and more  solar energy and in the long run it should aim at 
replacing the conventional source of energy with solar energy more so because 
conventional source of energy adds to the environmental pollution and global 
warming.  Since the setting up of a sola r power plant is capital intensive the 
Committee recommends that the Department should be adequately funded to enable  
it to attain its objective.  
8.3 Treatment for Diabetes 
 The Committee raised the specific issue of treatment of  Diabetes and desired to 
know the efforts the Department has taken to treat the disease which is afflicting a large 
section of the population of the country. The Department has st ated that it has identified 
the gene contribution of the Indian popula tion which causes Diabetes genetically. The 
Department also stated that a small diagnostic centre in co llaboration with the a private 
diagnostic company is being floated, where DSIR will provide the technology and also 
train the technicians to do the necessary tests after collecting blood samples. The 
Department will also create a  genomic diagnostic company of the CSIR to address the 
problem The technology used will reduce the cost of detection. The Department also 
informed that the multinational companies are not favouring it as it would reduce their 
profits. 
8.4 The Committee is of the view that the Department should invest substantially 
in establishing  technologies for the treatm ent of Diabetes which is afflicting a large 
portion of the Indian population regardle ss of age and also decreasing their work 
potential. The Committee feels that in case  the multinational companies are not in 
its favour, the Department can approach the Government aided hospitals, train 

their technichians and transfer the technol ogy, so that the poor  masses can avail of 
the cheaper alternative for the diagnosis of this disease. 
8.5 Development of Cheaper Computers 
   The Committee pointed out the fact th at the people are going in for Chinese  
made computers though the indigenous t echnology to produce cheap computers is 
available with the DSIR. The Department ha s stated that the CSIR has developed a 
simple computer for Rs 10,000/- only, but Go vernment departments/ private sector was 
not interested in investing cap ital for the project for larg e scale manufacture. However, 
the Department was ultimately able to sell the technology to Malaysia and is being 
marketed in Brazil and Malayasia. Further, the Chinese product is  popular because their 
Government takes the initia tive to popularize such products  internationally by giving 
subsidies so that the cost is reduced  and a huge market is created, while there is no such 
initiative on the part of our government. 
8.6 The Committee takes serious note of the fa ct that there is a lack of initiative 
on the part of the Government to promot e indigineous products, which is evident 
from the fact that none of the Government Departments or companies in the Private 
Sector were interested in the indigenous computer technology,  though it has been 
acknowledged internationally i.e. by Ma layasia and Brazil.  The Committee feels 
that injustice is being meted out to th e Indian scientists who developed the 
technology and will inevitably lower their morale and dissuade them from making 
such inventions in future. The Committee recommends that the Government should 
take the initiative to popularize such indigenous technologies and remove the 
bureaucratic hurdles which prevents such  innovative inventions from becoming 
realities and internationally competitive.

10. TECHNOLOGICAL  EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN 
10.1 The Committee took up the issue of  technological empowerment of women, 
which is one of the objectives of the Department and noted th at its performance has been 
quite disappointing and only 18% of the total scientists of the CSIR are women. Further, 
most of the women scientists are from th e elite and urban background implying that only 
these women are able to choose science as a career. The Department clarified that the 
percentage seems to be low but as compared to other scientific institutions such as the 
Indian Institutes of Technology( 4%), the Indian Institute of  Science(5%), CSIR has the 
highest percentage of women. The Department ha s also stated that it is trying to increase 
it upto 50%. As regards the background of wome n scientists, the Depa rtment has  stated 
that the section of women from poor backgr ound is progressively increasing in the CSIR. 

Women are being encouraged to join with sc hemes such as creches in every laboratory, 
flexible timings etc. 
10.2 The Committee is of the view that the country can progress only through 
social upliftment and the same can only be achieved by empowering the women with 
technological knowledge and ensuring their contribution in the field of science and 
also feels that a major limit ation for the girls to pursue science courses in the rural 
areas is the unavailability of these cour ses there. The Committee recommends  that 
the Government should promote science e ducation in rural areas and make special 
efforts to popularize it, specially amon g women. The Committee also recommends 
that an environment favourable to  women should be created in the laboratories to 
encourage them to join. Successful women sc ientists should be encouraged to reach 
out to women, specially from the rural area s to enthuse and enlighten girl students 
about the opportunities available in the scientific areas.  
11. CAREER PROSPECTS OF SCIENTISTS  
 On being enquired by the  Committee regarding the  career and promotional 
prospects of scientists in the CSIR laboratories, the Department has stated that presently a 
scientist is subjected to too many assessment stages for promotion, unlike other scientific 
institutions like IITs where there are compar atively less stages. Further sometimes the 
assessments itself are also delayed, which adds  to the frustration amongst the scientists. 
Steps have been initiated to bring the assessments upto date  which have yielded positive 
results. 
11.1   The Committee feels that if science in  India has to progre ss, the scientists 
have to be respected and provided prop er incentives through faster promotional 
avenues.  The Committee feels that burea ucratic hurdles such as delay in 
performance assessment should be strictly avoided to attract the best possible talent 
to join the organization. The Committee also recommends that the Department 
should take up the issue regarding improve ment in the pay scales of scientists 
vigorously with the government to ensure best possible career prospects for them.  
12. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY & TECHNOLOGY MANAGEMENT 
12.1 The Committee has been informed that the CSIR under the XIth Five Year Plan 
will meet the challenges of Intellectual Prope rty Rights (IPR) by selecting Public–Private 
partnerships (PPPs) & Research  & Development Projects. In  addition, continued efforts 
will be made to promote IPR through patent awareness and human resource development, 
patent acquisition portfolio, IP analysis as tool, prom oting techno-prenuership, and 
support to industry for innovation. The programme s proposed for the Eleventh Five Year 
Plan are listed below: 
 Filing, capturing, prosecution and ma intaining of IPR for CSIR R&D 
outputs; 
 Valuation and valorization of patent and IP portfolios; 
 Surveillance for infringement and enforcement of IPR; 
 Human Resource in IP cells of CSIR laboratories; and 
 Modernization of computing, communi cation and related facilities and 
infrastructure. 
12.2 The Department has informed that th e allocation for Intellectual Property & 
Technology Management has been decreased from Rs. 40.00 crores in B.E. and R.E. 
2009-2010 to Rs. 30.00 crores in B.E. 2010-2011. Stating the reasons, the department 
explained that the allocation for Intell ectual Property & Technology Management has 
been revised to Rs. 30.00 crores in view of th e fact that the filing of patent abroad has 
been restricted to commercially and strategica lly important inventions. In case there is 
any further requirement of budget, it will be reviewed during R.E. stage 2010-2011. The 

department also stated that the strategy of CSIR during the year 2009 -10  was to create 
greater awareness among CSIR la boratories in IPR and in the Eleventh Plan the strategy 
is focusing on to planned patenting.  
12.3 The Committee also enquired from the Depa rtment the reasons for the fact that  
despite a large number of patents application pending with DSIR, their 
conversion/development into workable tec hnology has been comparatively less. The 
Department has explained that  Patents are normally filed at the conceptual/ proof of 
concept stage, whereas the technology deve lopment is a complex and time consuming 
effort thereafter involves substantial investment in development activities. In case of drug 
development, for example, patents are filed at  initial stage when activity is established, 
lot of R&D goes thereafter before it reaches to clinical trial stage and the complete 
development of a drug involves an expens e of about one billion dollars. However, 
depending upon the nature of technology a nd field of application, development 
expenditure may vary. Therefore, Patents cannot  be construed as complete technologies. 
Worldwide, only about 3% to 4% patents are commercialized whereas  the CSIR’s patent 
utilization rate was comparatively higher at  8.67%. Further, CSIR has taken number of 
steps for creation of some features for an enabling ecosystem favorable for development 
and utilization of patentable products and pr ocesses. Some of the steps include equity 
partnership with IP devel opers and technology led manuf acturing firms & governmental 
support for such development efforts. 
12.4 The Committee appreciates the CSIR’s  patent utilization rate of 8.67% 
compared to worldwide statistics, but is st ill of the opinion th at due to lack of 
knowledge about Intellectual Property amon gst the researchers and a lack of an 
appropriate mechanism for transfer of the Intellectual Property a lot of research 
outcomes in universities, academic and res earch institutions, which hold potential 
for public good does not reach the i ndustry or the public and instead are 
languishing in the laboratories.  In some cases there has also  been delay in filing of 
patents specially as regards to our traditional knowledge and processes, on the part 
of our scientific institutions and other co untries have taken patents on the products 
and processes which had been traditiona lly used in our country for ages. The 
Committee therefore recomme nds that the Department should increase its focus 
towards the awareness of Intellectual Pr operty issues so that our traditional 
knowledge is well protected and also make  sincere efforts for optimal transfer and 
utilization of Intellectual Property from research institution to industry .

INITIATIVE(NMITLI)

viewed today as a benchmark of Public Pr ivate Partnership Schemes (PPP schemes) 
which is being emulated by various othe r government departments. The partners 
especially from the industry, were of the vi ew that industries which partnered NMITLI 
projects have highly benefited not only in terms of the hard object ives and achievements 
in the project wherein they participated but also in terms of other associated gains such as 
high quality technical inputs etc.   As India is entering in to a new era of R&D, more such 
newer approaches of innovation development need to be evolved and experimented.   
13.2  
 The Committee has been informed that the allocations made for 'New 
Millennium Indian Technology Leadership Initiative (NMITLI), has been decreased from                       
Rs.70.00 crores at B.E. to Rs. 50.00crores at  R.E. stage in 2009-2010 and then again

13.3 Informing the Committee of the successes achieved under the NMITLI Scheme,

viz. a new Tuberculosis molecule, a bio-therapeutic anti-b acterial molecule and a                 
anti-psoriasis(a skin disease) formulation. Se veral world class softwares in the area of 
Bio-informatics and monsoon prediction have been de veloped and are being marketed.          
A simple office computer and its varian ts costing around Rs.10,000/- have also been 
developed and are being marketed. An amb itious ‘bio-refinery concept’ based on 
sugarcane with the objective of substituti ng petroleum products as a base for many 
industrial chemicals is underway. NMITLI has embarked upon environment friendly 
bioprocesses for eliminating pollution from  tanneries wherein a large amounts of 
pollution causing industrial chemicals are used.  
13.4 The Committee expresses satisfaction  at the achievements of the New 
Millennium Indian Technology Leadership Initiative (NMITLI)   Scheme which 
seeks to encourage innovation centered scie ntific and technological developments 
and propel Indian industry towards a global leadership position, by utilizing the 
best available competencies of public fu nded R&D institutions, academia and 
private industry. The Committee also acknowle dges its appreciation at the fact that 
the NMITLI programme is being operated in diverse areas of technologies to yield 
cutting edge new technologies which are sust ainable and   eco-friendly such as ‘bio-
refinery concept’ or the bioprocesses for tanneries, which will help in reducing 
environmental pollution. The Committee feels that there is a lot of scope in the 
development of computer software arena and therefore recommends that the 
Department should vigorously pursue this field, and try to manufacture products 
such as the low cost Personal Computer which has a huge market. 
14. The Committee is of the view that the Department of Scientific & Industrial 
Research through its various research and development programmes is striving to 
uplift the standard of living in the country.  Keeping in vi ew the excellent work that 
the Department has undertaken, the kind of  competence it has exhibited and the 
kind of core and critical programmes it has envisaged for the future, the Committee 
strongly recommends that the Department  of Scientific & Industrial Research 
should be properly and adequately funded and any kind of reduction in outlay at 
R.E. stage should be strictly avoided.

REPORT 
Science and Technology is regarded as one  of the most powerful instruments of 
growth and development, especially in the emerging scenario of competitive economy like 
India. In the wake of the new demands of  the growing economy, Science and Technology 
system in the country is embarking on scienc e projects which have relevance to national 
needs and which will also be relevant fo r the future. The Department of Science & 
Technology plays a pivotal role in promotion of science & technology in the country and also 
catering to the country’s present and future needs in science.  
2. The Department of Science & Technology which was established in May, 1971 with 
the primary objective of promoting new areas of  Science and Technology, plays the role of a 
nodal department for organizing,  coordinating and promoting S& T activities in the country.  
The mandate given to the department includes, among others: 
 Formulation of policy statements and guidelines on Science and Technology 
(S&T); 
 Promotion of new areas of scientific research; 
 Co-ordination of inter-departmental S&T efforts; 
 Support basic and applied research in universities and other institutions; 
 International S&T Co-operation; 
 Support high quality research in au tonomous bodies where specialization 
ranges from advanced medical research materials to astronomy; 
 Catalyzing S&T interaction in societ al programmes and entrepreneurship 
development;  
 Science popularization, communication and S&T Management Information 
System; 
 Promotion of Commercialization of home grown technology; 
 Support to technology development program mes, technology information and 
assessment; and 
 Providing services in the areas of: 

(i) Surveying & Mapping (SOI and NATMO) 
(ii) Technology Developmen t and Application (TDB) 
3. ORGANISATIONAL  SETUP  
3.1 Department of Science and Technology is th e nodal Department of the Ministry of 
Science and Technology.  The Or ganisational Structure of the Department has evolved over 
the year to respond quickly to  the issues relating to the promotion and development of 
Science & Technology in the c ountry.  Broadly, the functions of the Department has been 
divided into Autonomous Institutes, Scie ntific Groups, Technology Development Board, 
Scientific Services besides the Administration and Integrated Finance divisions. There are 18 
Autonomous Institutes and 5 Science/Engi neering Academies/Associations, which are 
working in diverse areas for the promotion of Science and Technology. The Scientific 
Groups inter-alia consists of the Science & Engineering Research Council(SERC), National 
Council for Science & Technology Communica tion(NSCTC), National Resources Data 
Management System(NRDMS), Internatio nal Division, National Entrepreneurship 
Board(NEB), National Science and Tech nology Management Information System  
(NSTMIS). The Scientific Services has two subordinate offices, vi z., National Atlas and 
Thematic Mapping Organisation (NATMO) and Survey of India (SOI) under its 
administrative control. 
4. MECHANISM TO MONITOR AND REVIEW THE ONGOING SCHEMES 
4.1 The Department informed the Committee that it has a robust mechanism to monitor 
and review its ongoing schemes and programmes. Each of the programmes are reviewed and 
evaluated by subject expert committees on a continuous basis. The reviews and monitoring 
done by above committees are taken into account , before formulation and finalization of 
budgetary support. 
5.  ELEVENTH FIVE YEAR PLAN 
5.1 The   Department informed the Committee that  the total approved outlay for Xth Five 
Year Plan was Rs.3400.00 crores, against which actual expenditure incurred was Rs.3998.10 
crore.  The approved outlay fo r the Eleventh Five Year Pl an is Rs.11,028.00 crores against 
which actual expenditure incurred during 2007-08 and 2008-09 was         Rs. 1266.89 crores 
and Rs.1517.12 crores respectively. The provision proposed  in the               BE 2009-10 
under Plan is Rs.1775.00 crores, besides a provis ion of Rs.358.00 crores has been proposed 
under Non-Plan. Provision proposed in the BE 2010-11 under Plan is Rs.2025.00 crores, 
besides a provision of Rs.344.00 cror es under Non-Plan. The Department also informed that 
it was successful in achieving the projected target s of the Xth five year plan and in addition 
to the strengthening of the ongoing flagship programmes, some new in itiatives have been 
planned for the XIth Plan Peri od, recognizing the cha nging context of scie ntific enterprise 
and to meet present national needs, based on th e experience gained and looking at the future. 
The New major initiatives of the XIth Plan Period are described below: 
i) Formation of Science and En gineering Research Board:  A Science and 
Engineering Research Board has been set up to perform the functions & tasks of 
funding research and partner the DST in the development as well as promotional 
roles and will start functioning from April, 2010.  The formation of SERB 
represents a landmark. 
ii) Launch of Innovation in Science Pursui t for Inspired Research (INSPIRE) 
and Scholarships for Science in Higher Education (SHE) :            A major 
programme for attraction of talent from va rious sections of the society to opt for 
science as a career in research has been launched in December, 2008.  
iii) Promotion of University Research and Scientific Excellence (PURSE) : The 
Department, under infrastructure streng thening programmes, has mounted an 

initiative viz. the PURSE to provide incen tive grant system for universities based 
on the evidence of scientific publications during the period 1996-2006.  
iv) Launch of Cognition Science Init iative and Innovation Clusters:   DST has 
launched a Cognition Science Initiative a nd has selected tw o major nationally 
coordinated programmes on language learning and neural network. An Innovation 
Cluster is also being established under Public-Private Partnership.   
v) Security Technology Initiative:  A nationally coordinated initiative on S&T 
inputs to Security Technology has been co mmissioned with Indian Institute of 
Science as the implementing agency. 
vi) Water Technology Initiative: The Water technology in itiative of DST has 
focuses on various systems and solutions available for providing safe drinking 
water for domestic applications.  
vii) Establishment of Indian Beam line in  the Synchrotron in KEK, Japan:    A 
major step has been taken to establish an Indian beam line under Nano Mission, 
for materials science research in the S ynchrotron at Japan taking advantage of 
International S&T cooperation. This is a unique arrangement for promotion of 
basic research in materials science in the country. 
viii) Joining International Consortia on Facility for Anti-proton and Ion Research 
(FAIR): India has enrolled as a member of  an international consortium for 
establishment of FAIR and will be developing technologies and building 
instruments to global standards as a part of the consortium. 
ix) Establishment of New Institutes  and Centers under Nano mission: Institute 
for Nano Science and Technology is being established in Mohali as a part of 
Knowledge City and Centers are also  being established in Bangalore and Kolkata 
as a part of Nano mission. 
x) Establishment of Science Bridges and Support of Next Generation Telecom 
NetWork: DST has mounted science bridges with universities and research 
groups in UK and lead institutions in Indi a on reciprocity and partnership basis in 
collaboration with Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council 
(EPSRC), United Kingdom (UK). A total of  4 projects have been funded under 
Science Bridge and the next generation network has been selected for special 
funding. 
xi) Research Project support under stra tegic partnerships under European 
Union(EU)-India, Indo-UK, Indo-Australia, Indo-Israel, Indo-Canada 
programmes: Numerous budget intensive projects under bila teral and               
multilateral cooperation have been select ed after parallel peer review and 
supported under reciprocity and partners hip basis. The coordinated call for 
research on computer materials scien ce with European Union has been highly 
successful and new international partnerships are being set up. 
5.2 The Committee appreciates th e fact that the Department  has been successful in 
utilizing more amount during Xth Five Year  Plan i.e. Rs 3998.10 crores which is over 
and above the total outlay of Rs. 3400.00 crores. Acco rdingly, a sum of             Rs. 
588.00 crores more have been utilized in vario us schemes over the in itial total outlay 
provided during the Xth Five Year Plan. The Committee also appreciates the fact that 
some new initiatives have been planned for the XIth Plan Period in addition to the 
strengthening of the ongoing flagship pr ogrammes. The Committee has, however, 
observed that against the approved outlay of Rs.11,028.00 crores, the actual 
expenditure incurred by the Department on ye ar to year basis during the XIth Five 
Year Plan has been intimated as Rs 1266. 89 crores for the year 2007-08 and Rs.1517.12 
crores during 2008-09 of the Plan period, which seems to be on the lower side on annual 

basis, if the average annual expenditure in connection with the full utilization of the 
budget amount of Rs. 11,028.00 crores is concerned which comes to approximately Rs 
2000.00 crores per annum.  
5.3 The Committee has further noted that the provision proposed under B.E. for the 
year 2009-10 under plan expenditure is Rs 1775.00 crores, which is significantly higher 
than the actual expenditure made by the Department during 2007-08 and 2008-09. 
Again the Committee has noted that the pr ovision proposed under B.E. 2010-11 is Rs 
2025.00 crores under Plan expenditure which is Rs250.00 crores more than the 
provision proposed for the year 2009-10 under Plan expenditure. The Committee 
understands that this is a healthy trend as regards the allocation of funds for various 
schemes of the Department under B.E. The Committee also noted that the non-plan 
expenditure for the year 2009-10 was Rs 358. 00 crores and the same has been reduced 
to Rs.344.00  crores  at B.E. stage for the year 2010-11 i.e. a reduction of about Rs.14.00 
crores under the non-plan head. Given the aforesaid trend of expenditure and the 
allocation of amount by the Planning Commi ssion at B.E.stage as analysed in detail 
above, the Committee also hopes that the Department will make all out efforts to 
maintain its trend of achievements of ta rgets set in the XIth plan as well. The 
Committee hopes that the new initiatives like INSPIRE & PURSE would be able to 
attract the younger generations towards sc ience and the country would  forge new 
partnerships with the countries who are the global leaders in  science to attain the 
objective of transforming India into a technologically advanced hub. 
6.  BUDGETARY  ALLOCATION 
6.1 The Budgetary Estimates of the Departme nt of Science & Technology for the year 
2010-2011 are placed at Rs.2369.00 crores (Pla n Rs.2025.00 crores and Non-Plan Rs.344.00 
crores) as compared to last year’s B.E. and R.E. of Rs.2133.00 cr ores and Rs.2040.50 crores 
respectively.

Department  provided the following justification for additional funds sought by the 
Department during the year 2010-2011:- 
 DST is currently implementing a flagship programme namely, Innovation in 
Science Pursuit for Inspired Research (INSPIRE). This programme of the 
Department has just taken off and additional commitments of the scheme during

 Prime Minister’s Council has assigned two National Missions under National

 The Supreme Court has also ordered the De partment to find technical solutions to 
water problems. In pursuance to such order the Department has mounted a 
Technology Mission on Winning, Augm entation and Renovation (WAR) for 
water with a budget outlay of Rs.145.00 crores for two years. The Department has

 Science and Engineering Research Bo ard (SERB), an autonomous body for

6.4  The Committee has noted that under B.E. (Plan) expenditure for 2009-10

Again during 2010-11 the Department had proposed for a Plan allocation of                  
Rs 2300.00 crores for entire Department out of which Rs 2025.00 crores was actually 
allocated under B.E. Plan for 2010-11. The Co mmittee has, therefore, observed that

against the proposed demand for 2010-11 may affect the major programmes of the

for these crucial projects and will be detrimental to the growth of science and 
technology in the country in the long r un. The Committee theref ore recommends that 
the department may take up the issue of grea ter allotment of funds  strongly with the 
Planning Commission at the Revised Estimate stage.  
6.5 When enquired about the reduction in th e total outlay from Rs.2133.00 crores at the 
B.E. stage to Rs.2040.50 crores in R.E. stage in the year 2009-2010, the Department stated 
that though its overall expenditure wa s above the required bench mark at the             R.E. 
stage, but the pace of expenditure in few sc hemes was not found suitably desirable by the 
Ministry of Finance, hence there was a decrease in total out lay at the R.E. stage. However, 
the Department has stated that by February, 2010, it has been able to utilize 85% of the 
allocated budget for the year 2009-10 and the remaining 15% will be utilized by March, 
2010. 
6.6 The Committee expresses serious concern at the slow pace of expenditure in 
some schemes by the Department which lead to a reduction in allocation at the R.E. 
stage by the Ministry of Finance during the last financial year. The Committee is of the 
opinion that a higher proposed allocation ca n only be justified if the Department is 
more prompt and efficient in utilising th e already allocated funds under various 
schemes. The Committee therefore recommends th at the Department should do proper 
internal planning so that maximum expendi ture on its schemes could be  incurred 
before sending the proposals for Revised Esti mate stage. In this way the Ministry of 

Finance will not resort to cuts in expenditure at the R.E. stage in future as they have  
done in the present case. 
7.  NON-SUBMISSION OF THE ANNUAL REPORT FOR  
THE YEAR 2009-2010 
7.1 The Committee expressed its  strong dissatisfaction at the undue delay in the late 
submission of the Report for th e year 2009-2010 and the fact th at much of the data which 
have been provided, relate to the year 2008-20 09 or even an earlier period i.e. 2007-2008. 
Due to this, the Committee was unable to j udge the progress made by the Department and 
effectively evaluate the Budgetary allocati ons for the year 2009-2010. The Committee has, 
however, noted that the other Ministries/ Departments under its jurisdiction have been able to 
submit their Annual Reports for the year 2009-2010 to the Committee for its perusal.  
7.2 In resonse to the above, the Department expr essed regret at the delay in submission of 
the report for the year 2009-2010 and stated that  the draft Report has already been finalized 
and the final report would be submitted soon.  
7.3 The Committee takes note of  this serious lapse on the part of the Department 
which has lead to the non-submission of th e Annual Report of the Department for the 
year 2009-10 as a result of which the Committee fails to get a Comprehensive picture of 
the performance of various schemes under th e Department during the Plan period of 
2009-10. The Committee fails to understand while other Departments under the 
Ministry of Science & Technology, viz. DS IR & DBT have already submitted their 
annual reports in time, why DST has failed to  submit their Annual Report within the 
stipulated time frame.  The Committee, therefore, stri ctly recommends that the 
Department may draw up a comprehensive time schedule for the various stages 
involved in the preparation of the Annual Repo rt and strictly adhere to the targets set 
in the schedule so that the Annual Reports are printed and submitted to the Committee 
well within the time limit.  The Department may also examine and analyse the approach 
followed by the other Departments of the Ministry of Science & Technology, which 
have submitted their reports in time and ad opt an effective method for the preparation 
of its Annual Reports for the next Plan period of 2010-11. 
MAJOR PROGRAMMES OF THE DEPARTMENT

Research Council (SERC).  The objectives of the SERC are:-

activities.

Rs.572.00 crores at B.E. for the year 2010-2011. E xplaining the reasons fo r the increase the 
Department stated that it is committed to th e pursuit and promotion of science & technology 
with vigor in the 11
th Five year plan. SERC, which is the single largest basic research 
funding body in the country across  disciplines and ac ross institutions, ha s intensified the 
R&D promotional activities through innovative programmes su ch as ‘Intensification of 
Research in High Priority Ar eas’ (IRHPA), Fund for Improvement  of S&T Infrastructure in 
Universities and Higher Educational Institutions  (FIST), Fast Track Young Scientist’s R&D 

programme and Prestigious Fellowship awar ds viz. J.C. Bose, Ramanujan, Ramanna 
Fellowships, etc.

B.E. 2010-2011 compared to the allocation of Rs. 537.00 crores in 2009-2010 is primarily to 
undertake major R&D activities under the Scie nce & Engineering Rese arch Board (SERB) 
and to accommodate expanding research in infrastructural developmental activities such as 
special regional packages (North Eastern Region, Jammu & Kashmir and Bihar) under the 
FIST programme. This moderate  allocation would suffice to meet the increasing importance 
of indigenous Research & Development. The Committee was also informed that the SERB, 
which has been created recently after efforts by the Department spanning over 26 years, will 
take over the entire funding role of the Department besides the policy making and 
promotional roles of the Department from April, 2010.  
8.4 The Committee is of the opinion that the core responsibility of the Department is 
to promote basic and applied research in ne wly emerging and frontier areas of science 
and build up necessary infrastructure for the purpose. The Committee appreciates the 
initiative of the Department in  expanding research in infrastructural developmental 
activities in Universities and Higher Educat ional Institutions in states which lack 
necessary scientific infrastructure,  thro ugh special regional packages in the North 
Eastern Region, the states of  Jammu & Kashmir and Bihar.  The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the Planning Commission should adequately fund such special 
initiatives of the Department for encouragi ng the research and development activities, 
so that the same can be pursued with vigour.  
8.5 The Committee appreciates the efforts of the Department which have been 
directed towards the creation of the Scienc e & Engineering Research Board (SERB) 
which will be engaged in the role of en tire funding of various research projects 
undertaken by the Department. The Commit tee feels that this is a major step 
undertaken by the Department to finance various  projects in a focused and well–
coordinated manner.  
8.6 PUBLICATIONS/ JOURNAL S OF THE DEPARTMENT 
In reply to a query regarding the publicati on of more than 1500 journals/publications 
by the SERC and the mechanism adopted by th e Department for such publications, the 
Committee was informed that the Department supports individual scientists and not the 
institutions. A proposal is submitted by the concer ned scientist, which is then scrutinized by 
five reviewers who are specialists in the area.  After atleast three of the reviewers submit a 
report in favour of the proposal, a presentation is made before a Committee, after which the 
journal is selected for publica tion. In reply to a nother query, regarding the quality of the 
publications, the Department informed that an  international group grad es the publications 
throughout the world depending upon a systema tic method of giving numbers called the 
Impact Factor(IF).  
8.7 The Committee was also informed that in the past the universi ties and the research 
laboratories used to contribute equally i.e. 50% each, towards the publication of research 
journals/publications. However of late, only 15 % contribution comes from the Universities, 
while 50% comes from the Research Laboratorie s and rest from other sources. Therefore the 
contribution of the Universities have gone dow n. The Department is therefore trying to 
increase the contribution through incentive mech anisms like giving grants to the Universities 
which publish journals/publications. 
8.8   The Committee expresses serious concern  about the fact that the contribution 
of the Universities as regards publication of  research papers/journals have decreased 
over the years from an initial 50% to current figure of 15%, despite the fact that there 
has been incentive grant system for Universit ies, based on the evidence of scientific 

publications during the period from 1996-2006 under PURSE programme and also 
despite the fact that there has been an ove rall increase in funds allocation towards 
science and technology which essentially is  not a favourable indication so far as 
performance of  Science & Technology in the country is concerned. The Committee 
therefore recommends that the Department sh ould evolve a more effective incentive 
mechanism to encourage the Universities to augment their contribution in terms of  
publications of quality research papers/journals.  
8.9 The Committee also feels that the Impa ct Factor of published journals and 
research papers in the country is low as co mpared to other advanced countries who are 
global leaders in the field of science & t echnology. The Committee is of the opinion that 
the Impact Factor is correlated with the quality  of the research papers/journals  i.e. the 
degree of originality involved and also ho w it reflects about basic research on a 
particular issue. Since the basic research is  persistently neglected in the country, the 
Impact Factor of the Indian journals a nd research papers in science is globally 
languishing behind. Therefore, the Committ ee feels that more emphasis on basic 
research needs to be made so that internat ional quotation from Indian journals could 
be increased in future. Apart from this, the Committee is of the firm opinion that unless 
Indian pioneering research publications/papers get world-wide online publicity, the 
Impact Factor will always remain poor. The Committee, therefore, suggests that 
adequate steps may be taken to give wid er international publicity to Indian science 
journals/ research papers in future.

stronger relations both at bilateral and mult i-lateral levels which are inevitable to

Pharmaceuticals Industry towards development of new drugs in all systems of Medicine.

     To synergise the strengths of publicly funded R&D inst itutions and Indian 
Pharmaceutical Industry in developing drugs in areas of national relevance. 
     To create an enabli ng, infrastructure, mechanisms a nd linkages to facilitate new 
drug development. 
     To stimulate skill development of human resources in  R&D for drugs and 
pharmaceuticals. 
12.2 The Committee noted that the allocation made to 'Drugs and Pharmaceutical 
Research' has been reduced from Rs.96.00 crores in B.E. to Rs.78.00 crores in R.E. in the 
year 2009-2010 and then again drastically reduced to Rs.50.00 crores in B.E. 2010-2011. The

11th Five Year Plan by Planning Commission and after considering several new schemes and 
programmes relating to Drugs & Pharmaceuti cal Research implemented by the various 
Departments/agencies such as Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Department of AYUSH,
